item.content:encoded:
Dalton Rushing’s breakout season has not exactly gone to plan for himself or the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The upstart catcher got his first taste of extended play in the wake of Will Smith spending much of the first half of the season on the injured list.
Rushing impressively has clubbed 12 homers in only 250 plate appearances. As his confidence grew, the Dodgers faced the reality that Rushing needed to play multiple times a week — even if that meant mixing in starts at first base along with his duties behind the plate.
Unfortunately for Rushing, his season became derailed on Aug. 3. Reports initially focused around a partially torn UCL in his elbow. However, as Rushing recently told Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times, that had been a preexisting injury he had been playing through since 2022.
Instead, it’s actually a flexor strain which has sidelined the catcher. Rushing is hoping that he can still be an impact player for the ballclub with the postseason right around the corner.
He's also hoping to avoid offseason surgery.
“I’m pretty confident I can still avoid surgery after the shot,” Rushing said. “Obviously, when I re-injured it the second time, I was almost 70-30, thinking that I was for sure going to need surgery. But after I got the shot and it ran its course, I feel as close to healthy in my arm as I have in a pretty long time.”
Rushing is projected to be activated at some point this week. With only a few games remaining on the schedule, the Dodgers will determine whether he can be a threat off the bench solely as a hitter.
With Miguel Rojas and Kiké Hernandez occupying two of the team’s bench spots on a hypothetical roster, the need for a left-handed bat is there.
At this point, Rushing is likely battling with phenom Josue De Paula for a spot on the roster for the first round. De Paula was fantastic in his brief stint in the big leagues — before being sent down on Wednesday — hitting .323 with a whopping 11 walks to just five strikeouts.
Where Rushing has the obvious edge is in collective experience. He likely won’t be able to catch even in an emergency role, though.
Having said that, as someone that can provide pop from the left side, the Dodgers will have to weigh whether experience wins out over a very young yet gifted rookie with less than 50 at-bats at the major league level.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Jason Fray is a Los Angeles native with 10+ years of professional experience in the sports media world. A graduate of UCLA, Fray has written previously for the likes of Bleacher Report, FOX Sports, Saturday Down South, MSN, Dodgers Nation, Sports Illustrated and Newsweek.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: What Dave Roberts said about Shohei Ohtani's 1st game back from IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Los Angeles Dodgers designated hitter Shohei Ohtani returned to the lineup Wednesday after spending two weeks on the injured list.
Ohtani was activated before Los Angeles' 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres after missing time because of left knee soreness and right biceps discomfort. It was his first game since Sept. 7, and he was inserted into the No. 2 spot against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
The 32-year-old finished 1-for-4 with a walk and two strikeouts. His first at-bat ended with a 99 mph single to right field, and he later hit a 384-foot flyout to center. His biggest missed opportunity came in the fourth inning, when he struck out with the bases loaded during the Dodgers' best scoring chance.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Despite the result, manager Dave Roberts came away encouraged by what he saw from Ohtani.
"He looked good. I thought the at-bat quality was good," said Roberts. "There wasn't any chase. I thought he hit the ball hardest in his first at-bat. It's been a while since he's played in a game, but it just felt like he wasn't sped up at all."
In his final games before landing on the IL, Ohtani had appeared physically compromised at the plate, including moments when he shook out his arm and winced. Los Angeles placed him on the injured list on Sept. 9 after trying to manage the lingering issues while keeping him available.
Ohtani had begun his hitting program about a week before Wednesday's return and had recently faced simulated pitching. He had entered his last game before the IL stint batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs, 89 runs and 80 walks through 134 games.
Roberts said Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Thursday for the series finale. The Dodgers are also still evaluating their batting order against left-handed pitching for the postseason. Against right-handers, Roberts said he would likely put Ohtani back in the leadoff spot and move Mookie Betts to No. 2.
Betts had occupied the leadoff role while Ohtani was away and was batting .366 with six homers, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs in 18 September games.
Ohtani won't take the mound in the playoffs, making his health at the plate all the more important as October approaches.
Related: Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal set to return to Dodgers

item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen

item.content:encoded:
Back when Will Smith's wife, Cara, taught first grade at a Title I school in Kentucky, she saw firsthand how many of her students did not have access to the resources they needed for success, whether at home or at school. Through her, it opened Smith's eyes to an area where he could one day make a difference.
In 2021, Cara and Will Smith founded the Catching Hope Foundation, which has been a presence in the Los Angeles community ever since. In recognition of the foundation's work, Will Smith was the Dodgers' nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award.
"It's a huge honor," Smith said. "I think Roberto's legacy is incredible. Obviously incredible baseball career, but more importantly, the stuff he did off the field. You know, he's 1A in that regard, doing things for other people and making other people's lives better."
The Roberto Clemente Award is one of Major League Baseball's highest honors, given annually to the player who best represents the game through extraordinary character, community involvement, philanthropy and positive contributions on and off the field.
One player from each team is nominated for the award, and the overall winner is determined by a blue-ribbon panel that includes a fan vote, which is open until Sunday. The winner will be honored during the 2026 World Series.
Mookie Betts won last year's Roberto Clemente Award, joining Justin Turner (2022), Clayton Kershaw (2012) and Steve Garvey (1981) as the fourth Dodger to win the league-wide honor. Smith could become the fifth, but for him, being able to use his platform for good is reward enough.
"We really enjoy brightening kids' days and helping them out and getting them on their feet, or just giving them opportunities that they probably wouldn't have had unless we step in and provide it," Smith said. "It's super important to us just because we feel like it's the right thing to do. We have an opportunity to help people and just enjoy it."
The Catching Hope Foundation states that its mission is "to help underprivileged children with critical skills needed for leadership, self-advocacy, and self-sufficiency." The aim is to allocate resources to students in need that will help them develop valuable tools for success.
To that end, the Catching Hope Foundation has entered into longer-term partnerships with multiple schools, beginning with Clifford Elementary School in 2024. The relationship began with an L.A. Reads Storytime event and continued across two school years, ending with the installation of a permanent outdoor literacy space as part of a 2024 World Series Legacy Initiative in partnership with the Dodgers and MLB.
In 2025, the Catching Hope Foundation partnered with two additional schools -- Manhattan Place Elementary School in South L.A. and Langdon Elementary School in the San Fernando Valley -- which also received outdoor literacy areas. As the relationships with each school blossomed, Smith and his foundation have gained a deeper understanding into how to best serve each community.
The Smiths work with school districts to identify which schools have the greatest needs, whether they be related to funding, student performance or external circumstances. Following the devastating 2025 Southern California wildfires, they partnered with the Los Angeles Unified School District Foundation and the Pasadena Unified School District Foundation to auction off the 2024 World Series final out ball, donating $180,000 in proceeds to the districts.
In April of this year, the Catching Hope Foundation visited one of the impacted LAUSD schools, Marquez Charter Elementary School, which burned down in the Palisades Fire but has since reopened. Students from Marquez Charter were later invited to Dodger Stadium for the Catching Hope Community Clinic, an annual event that hosts a different elementary school each year.
"We like trying to build a relationship with the schools and really get to know them and what they need and what's truly going to help the kids," Smith said. "Not, we're offering one thing to the school that might not need it. It's, no, what do you really need for the school that's really going to help encourage kids to show up and learn and be happy and just enjoy school and learning, and to set them up the rest of their lives?"
As a catcher, Smith builds relationships with the members of his pitching staff on a daily basis. That ability plays a big role in his work with the community, too.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers exec confirms Shohei Ohtani suspicions as injuries potentially impact playoff impact
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: In hindsight, Andrew Friedman made the Dodgers’ handling of Shohei Ohtani’s injury-plagued season this year sound rather simple. Throughout Ohtani’s return to a full-time two-way role, the team’s president of baseball operations said, the Dodgers checked in with the superstar “on a daily basis, a weekly basis” to monitor how he was feeling as he handled both pitching and hitting duties. That process intensified once Ohtani began battling left knee and right arm injuries in the middle of the seas
item.content:encoded:
In hindsight, Andrew Friedman made the Dodgers’ handling of Shohei Ohtani’s injury-plagued season this year sound rather simple.
Throughout Ohtani’s return to a full-time two-way role, the team’s president of baseball operations said, the Dodgers checked in with the superstar “on a daily basis, a weekly basis” to monitor how he was feeling as he handled both pitching and hitting duties.
That process intensified once Ohtani began battling left knee and right arm injuries in the middle of the season, leading both to the decision to remove Ohtani from the starting rotation in early July –– but also to let him continue playing through his ailments as the team’s everyday DH while attempting to ramp back up with a pitching program, as well.
It all reached a tipping point two weeks ago, when a clearly diminished Ohtani was finally placed on the injured list amid a 6-for-52 batting slump, and had any plans of returning to the mound this season scuttled for good.
And now, continuing such dialogue will be crucial over the rest of the campaign, with Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday for a postseason push that he and the team hopes will see the 32-year-old slugger rediscover his typical productivity at the plate.
“The most important thing is how much better he feels,” Friedman said, speaking to reporters before Ohtani’s 1-for-4 performance in a loss to the San Diego Padres. “Now, it’s about continuing that as he takes game-intensity at-bats.”
How Ohtani and the Dodgers reached this point, of course, has been the subject of much speculation and criticism over recent weeks.
From the start of the year, the club’s No. 1 priority was having Ohtani at full strength as a hitter entering the playoffs.
That they failed in that endeavour –– even Friedman acknowledged Wednesday that Ohtani probably isn’t back to 100% physically, though also insisted that “Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great” –– will be the source of significant retrospection within the organization.
Especially if a compromised Ohtani prevents the Dodgers from winning a third-consecutive World Series this fall.
“There’s no question [the injuries] affected him,” Friedman said. “I think the fact that he feels as good as he does right now is certainly encouraging. Now it’s about making sure that holds.”
Friedman didn’t assign blame for why Ohtani’s season went so wrong. He didn’t second-guess the team’s decision to let him play with his injuries for as long as they did, nor Ohtani’s insistence on trying to try and push through his physical problems.
Every time the sides met to discuss Ohtani’s usage, Friedman said, “his answer has been whatever it takes to help the team win. It legitimately has been that single time.”
The one dynamic Friedman did emphasize upon reflection, however, was whether Ohtani was honest enough with himself about how much his health had deteriorated.
“He’s not always the best reporter of how he feels,” Friedman said. “Freddie [Freeman is] the same way. Clayton Kershaw. I’ve been around a lot of these guys that feel like their job is to be out there to help the team however they can, and sometimes will downplay some things that are bothering them.”
In a vacuum, that isn’t necessarily a bad thing.
Friedman said he had “respect” for Ohtani’s dedication to post as often as possible. He recognized that, “in his mind, he thought the best way to help the team was to go out and play.”
At this point, though, it’s hard not to wonder whether Ohtani pushed himself too hard –– and that the team wasn’t proactive enough in stopping him from doing so.
“I think in his mind, he just thought that what he was dealing with was more minor,” Friedman said, while cutting Ohtani some slack by noting he never received more significant diagnoses than inflammation in both his knee and arm.
“Again, the communication back and forth has been awesome,” Friedman added. “The fully sharing exactly how he’s feeling, maybe not as awesome.”
It has certainly left the Dodgers in a less-than-awesome spot now, uncertain of exactly what version of Ohtani they will get over a grueling October trek.
This week, Friedman said the Dodgers want to get Ohtani “as many at-bats as we can” so he can build “some rhythm and timing” with his swing. However, he also didn’t commit to Ohtani playing all five of the team’s remaining games, wanting to see how he handles his return to action first (Wednesday’s performance, at least, offered some signs of progress).
It means, in the coming weeks, more daily check-ins will continue between Ohtani and the Dodgers.
At this point, it’s the best they can do to manage his health entering the playoffs.
As for the past?
“He was in a good enough spot to help us win,” Friedman said, “and we agreed with that.”

「ドジャース１－５パドレス」（２３日、ロサンゼルス）
ドジャースの山本由伸投手（２８）は６回４失点で９敗目を喫した。それでも自責点２で、ＭＬＢ単独トップとなる２２度目のクオリティースタート（６回以上、自責点３以下）を達成。「うれしく思いますし、またそういうことができるように頑張ります」と、力を込めた。
大谷の復帰についても言及。一緒にゲームに出場したことで「同じ試合に出られてうれしいし、チームメートも同じだと思います。何よりファンの方がうれしいと思いますし、とにかくよかった」と語った。
今回がレギュラーシーズン最後の登板となり、今後はポストシーズンに向け調整する。昨季のワールドシリーズは獅子奮迅の活躍でＭＶＰを獲得。３連覇に向け「今も去年も調子よくシーズンを終われた。体の調子も良くてしっかり準備できると思う」と語っていた。

item.title: [TheWrap] Los Angeles Dodgers' Mookie Betts Signs With 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment
item.dc:creator: Loree Seitz
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts has signed with 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment for personal representation. Under the new representation structure, the firms will spearhead the four-time World Series champion’s personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development. The partnership comes as the eight-time MLB All-Star and entrepreneur hopes to expand his business footprint off the field, with both 3 Arts Sports and SSE focused on his personal branding and busi
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts has signed with 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment for personal representation.
Under the new representation structure, the firms will spearhead the four-time World Series champion’s personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development.
The partnership comes as the eight-time MLB All-Star and entrepreneur hopes to expand his business footprint off the field, with both 3 Arts Sports and SSE focused on his personal branding and business endeavors. It marks a shift in Betts’ career as he focuses on long-term creative ownership and global brand expansion.
“Mookie Betts is a generational talent on the field and an incredibly forward-thinking entrepreneur off it. We are thrilled to collaborate across sports and entertainment to build a comprehensive strategy for one of baseball’s most enduring icons,” 3 Arts Entertainment co-CEO Brian Weinstein and SSE founder and president Doug Sanders said in a joint statement. “This partnership aligns with Mookie’s ambitious vision by tapping into our respective teams’ expertise and industry relationships.”
Betts joins the 3 Arts Sports roster alongside sports stars that have shaken up the pop culture scene, including Travis Kelce, the WNBA’s Sophie Cunningham and NFL star Jayden Daniels.
“I’ve always believed in surrounding myself with people who understand my vision and bring expertise in areas where I can continue to grow,” Betts said. “As the opportunities around me have continued to evolve, it felt important to build a specialized team that could help me navigate and develop those opportunities the right way. I’m excited to have 3 Arts Sports and SSE alongside me and to have the right people in place to support everything I’m building off the field.”

item.title: [nypost.com] Shohei Ohtani is back — but something doesn’t look right with Dodgers star

item.content:encoded:
Something’s not right.
The Dodgers said so without saying so.
When Shohei Ohtani returned from the 15-day injured list, they batted him second.
This is no knock on Mookie Betts, who led off instead. Betts is an eight-time All-Star who is hitting .317 over his last 42 games, but Ohtani is, well, Ohtani.
Ohtani is the best player in baseball when healthy, or even close to healthy. If the Dodgers believed Ohtani could be that player for them in the postseason, they wouldn’t have moved him out of his customary spot in the order, and it wouldn’t have mattered how anyone else on their team was hitting or whether the opposing pitcher was right- and left-handed.
Presumably, the Dodgers had more insights into his injured right arm and left knee than they shared.
Which is why enthusiasm over Ohtani’s performance on Wednesday should be tempered.
Without question, Ohtani looked better in the 5-1 loss to the San Diego Padres than he did the last time he played.
That didn’t mean he was back to playing like himself – or that he will be at any time during the playoffs.
The return of a Most Valuable Player can have transformative effects on a team, especially if that Most Valuable Player is as healthy as the Dodgers claimed Ohtani was after resting for two-plus weeks, but President of Baseball Operations Andrew Friedman and manager Dave Roberts both spent time before the game managing expectations.
Asked which version of Ohtani was coming back to the team, Friedman replied, “I mean, these aren’t things there’s a clear answer to.”
Roberts said he wanted to see Ohtani “being controlled, taking good at-bats.”
By that standard, Ohtani’s first game back was a massive triumph.
In the first inning, Ohtani singled off left-hander Robbie Ray on the kind of low pitch he was physically incapable of reaching two or three weeks earlier because of his knee problem.
Ohtani later drove a high 99-mph fastball to the warning track, prompting Dodgers broadcaster Joe Davis to scream: “That is a majestic fly ball!”
“I think if you look back at the last couple weeks when he was active, he wasn’t getting to that pitch,” Roberts said of the four-seamer upstairs from right-hander Bradgley Rodriguez.
For the most part, Ohtani didn’t swing at pitches outside of the strike zone. He worked two-ball counts in each of his first four plate appearances, and drew a walk in the third inning.
The Dodgers would almost certainly take games like this from Ohtani. Regardless of what he actually was and wasn’t able to do, the Padres viewed him as a threat, and that alone made him a presence in the lineup.
Ohtani has acknowledged he was unlikely to be 100% healthy again this season, but maintaining an aura of danger will require him to not return to where he was physically leading up to his IL stint.
“Shohei says he feels back to where he was earlier in the year, which is great, which is a good start,” Friedman said. “Now, it’s one thing to feel that way for any player coming back from the IL. When you’re coming back, now the question is, as you start to load on real games and that intensity and that workload, it’s making sure that what we’re done keeps guys in position to be at their best.”
Or, in this case, to at least be viewed as a threat.
Roberts previously described Ohtani as “pain-free” but acknowledged he was still dealing with “discomfort you can play through.” The Dodgers have already seen what happens when Ohtani plays too many games with his arm and knee problems, and every game he plays theoretically pushes him closer to the stage at which the pain becomes unbearable.
How close is Ohtani to that point?
Was the usually-aggressive Ohtani as patient as he was in the batter’s box because he wanted to protect his arm by limiting his swings?
Did his warning-track drive not clear the outfield wall because he hit the ball with the end of his bat or because he wasn’t at full strength?
What should be made of the two at-bats in which he struck out? With the bases loaded, two outs and the count full in the fourth inning, Ohtani was late on a 98.5-mph sinker by David Morgan. In the ninth, Ohtani looked as if he had no chance against closer Mason Miller, who struck him out on three pitches.
Ohtani wasn’t made available to answer any of these questions. By the time the clubhouse opened to reporters, Ohtani was gone.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Earns Rave Reviews From Dodgers Leadership
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula is no longer on the active roster after getting sent down to Triple-A, but the major league team had nothing but positive things to say. De Paula played just 11 games with the Dodgers, but he delivered outstanding offensive production and quickly earned the fanbase’s adoration as a young presence at the plate. However, he was demoted as Shohei Ohtani neared activation from the injured list. Fans who bought into what the 21-year-old showed were disa
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Josue De Paula is no longer on the active roster after getting sent down to Triple-A, but the major league team had nothing but positive things to say.
De Paula played just 11 games with the Dodgers, but he delivered outstanding offensive production and quickly earned the fanbase’s adoration as a young presence at the plate.
However, he was demoted as Shohei Ohtani neared activation from the injured list. Fans who bought into what the 21-year-old showed were disappointed, but the organization seemed just as reluctant to see him go.
What the Dodgers think of De Paula
After the move was announced, manager Dave Roberts said De Paula, as the team’s default designated hitter, was set to lose at-bats now that Ohtani returned.
Still, De Paula earned a postseason look, and the team will factor him into its plans.
“We had a runway to give him, which we gave him, and he performed more than admirably. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night,” Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
In terms of skill set, Roberts sees all of De Paul’s traits — the plate approach, swing decision, and vision to deliver in the postseason.
“He’s just a special hitter,” Roberts added. “Hitters don’t see the ball that quickly out of hand; it’s a gift. Just the ability to [limit] chase, I think that lines up in the postseason. And no moment is going to be too big for that kid.”
De Paula’s impressive numbers
Through 11 games in the big leagues, De Paul is hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS. He is getting on base during half of his plate appearances, and he is really making hitters work.
Andrew Friedman, the president of baseball operations, had been following De Paula closely, and despite the otherworldly production, the Dodgers executive was not surprised.
“It’s what you expect, but you never really know until you see it,” Friedman said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“But it obviously really stood out, and he’s done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we’re making our postseason roster.”
Meanwhile, Josue De Paula gets the chance to show what he can do defensively in Triple-A while the Dodgers decide.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dodgers' push for first-round bye, favorable playoff schedule means more for Miguel Rojas
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have already punched their ticket to the postseason and rule the NL West once again, but there's a final frontier that eluded them in 2025. They're cusp on clinching a first-round bye in the National League over the Atlanta Braves; a win for the Dodgers or a loss for the Braves on Thursday would lock it up for LA.
The Dodgers would surely love a few days off between the end of the regular season and the start of the NLDS, given how banged up the roster is right now. Shohei Ohtani, Dalton Rushing, and Blake Snell are just a few of their recently injured players who could use a little more time to prepare.
Miguel Rojas would also love to not have to work on October 1, but not because of an injury. According to Bill Plunkett of the Orange County Register, Rojas is scheduled to take his US citizenship test on the same day as a potential Game 3 of the Wild Card series. Rojas is looking to follow in the footsteps of Cincinnati Reds slugger — and fellow Venezuela native — Eugenio Suárez, who passed his citizenship test this season, who passed earlier this month.
The Dodgers would love to have Miguel Rojas for every game of the playoffs
Even if the Dodgers were to fall into the Wild Card, they would host all three of those games at Dodger Stadium, but that could still complicate Rojas' participation in that series. LA could always leave him off the Wild Card roster and bring him back for the NLDS, but he's been on almost every Dodgers postseason roster since he returned to the team in 2023. The only exception was the NLDS in 2024, when he sat with injury.
Rojas has been working in the United States since 2010, when the Reds signed him as an international free agent, but his family still lives in his home country. Earlier this season, he declined a move to the bereavement list after his father passed away in Venezuela, and his wife and children were in Caracas during the devastating earthquakes the country suffered in June.
He's set to retire at the end of the season but has major league coaching and managerial aspirations, so staying in the United States after his playing career makes sense.
Barring disaster, the Dodgers' schedule should be clear to let Rojas take the next step toward US citizenship. Dodgers fans are surely wishing Miggy the best of luck.

They are coming off a 5-1 loss on Wednesday night.
Dodgers Announced Dalton Rushing Update
This week, the Dodgers announced the latest update on Dalton Rushing.
He has been out since September 5 with an injury.
MLB.com wrote (on September 22): “Could be activated before the end of the regular season so that the Dodgers can evaluate him as a bench option. He will only be a hitter.”
Before getting hurt, Rushing had been batting .249 with 55 hits, 12 home runs, 36 RBIs and 37 runs in 78 games.
Rushing was picked in the 2nd round of the 2022 MLB Draft.
He is in the middle of his second season in the MLB (all with the Dodgers).
Looking At The Dodgers Right Now
The Dodgers have had another fantastic season.
They are currently 97-61 with a 158 games.

item.content:encoded:
3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment have partnered to sign Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts for personal representation.
The signing comes at a time when the Dodgers have clinched a playoff spot for a 14th consecutive season. Betts has been playing as shortstop this season.
Under this new representation structure, 3 Arts Sports and SSE will co-manage personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development for the four-time World Series champion, eight-time All-Star and former American League MVP.
"Mookie Betts is a generational talent on the field and an incredibly forward-thinking entrepreneur off it. We are thrilled to collaborate across sports and entertainment to build a comprehensive strategy for one of baseball's most enduring icons," said Brian Weinstein, co-CEO of 3 Arts Entertainment, and Doug Sanders, Founder & President of SSE. "This partnership aligns with Mookie's ambitious vision by tapping into our respective teams' expertise and industry relationships."
More from Deadline
"I've always believed in surrounding myself with people who understand my vision and bring expertise in areas where I can continue to grow," said Betts. "As the opportunities around me have continued to evolve, it felt important to build a specialized team that could help me navigate and develop those opportunities the right way. I'm excited to have 3 Arts Sports and SSE alongside me and to have the right people in place to support everything I'm building off the field."
This representation structure marks a unified effort to maximize Betts' impact both as a global athlete and an entrepreneur. 3 Arts Sports and SSE will focus on his personal brand, endorsements and business endeavors.
The Nashville, TN-born Betts was drafted by the Boston Red Sox in 2011 and made his MLB debut in the 2014 season, where he played second base and outfield. He soon became the Red Sox center fielder in 2014 moving to right field in 2016, helping them win the World Series in 2018 when he won the AL MVP award. In 2020, after six seasons with Boston, Betts was traded to the Dodgers and signed a 12-year, $365 million extension with the team through the 2032 season.
Betts counts 22 home runs this season with 68 RBIs.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Will Smith continued to show encouraging signs at the plate Wednesday night, collecting a single and drawing two walks in the Dodgers’ 5-1 loss to the Padres. The catcher worked lengthy at-bats throughout the evening, something he hopes will carry over into October.
Asked about his approach as the postseason draws closer, Smith emphasized the importance of remaining selective and making opposing pitchers work.
“Just trying to swing at the right pitches, take the right pitches, foul good pitches off,” Smith said. “Just trying to take one good at-bat at a time.”
With San Diego representing a possible postseason opponent, Smith was also asked whether the potential for another October meeting changes how the Dodgers approach their remaining regular-season games.
His answer was straightforward.
“No, we’re still approaching it trying to win ballgames,” he said. “I don’t think we’ve clinched the bye yet, so we’re still trying to do that.”
Wednesday’s loss delayed the Dodgers’ opportunity to secure that coveted first-round bye, but Smith indicated that the team’s confidence remains intact. He emphasized that the players have maintained a consistent outlook throughout the season, recognizing that individual losses are inevitable while keeping their larger objective in mind.
“Just one day at a time,” Smith said. “We’re not going to win every game. We still believe in each other day in and day out to win a ballgame and to reach our goal of winning the World Series again.”
With October approaching, Smith and the Dodgers remain focused on securing their postseason position before turning their attention to defending their championship.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres will say farewell for now in their final meeting of the regular season Thursday night in L.A., with one team guaranteed to celebrate at the end of the evening.
In the finale of the next-to-last series for each team, the Padres have a magic number of one for clinching a National League wild-card spot, while the Dodgers have a magic number of one to earn a top-two seed in the playoffs and a bye into a division series matchup.
There even remains a chance that both achieve their objectives depending on other results throughout the NL.
As it stands now, the Dodgers (97-61) and Padres (88-70) could collide again in a division-series matchup. The Padres earned a 5-1 victory Wednesday to end the Dodgers’ 11-game home winning streak, while the Dodgers won 7-0 on Tuesday.
The Padres have won 14 of their past 16 games.
A pair of right-handers will match up in the final game of the series as San Diego sends Nick Pivetta (3-2, 3.30 ERA) to the mound, while Los Angeles will counter with Tyler Glasnow (5-1, 3.46).
Pivetta will have history on the line. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons. In three starts since a five-month stint on the injured list because of a right elbow flexor strain, Pivetta is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA.
In eight career appearances against the Dodgers (seven starts), he is 1-2 with a 3.62 ERA.
Pivetta has yet to go more than five innings since his return, but he will have additional bullpen support with the return of right-hander Jason Adam, who has been out since June with a shoulder injury.
“What this team’s doing is really special,” Adam said, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. “I just want to fill my role, however that looks, and help them win ballgames. We’ve seen that this team’s good with or without me. I just want to do my part to contribute.”
The Dodgers saw Shohei Ohtani return from a biceps injury Wednesday, and he reached base in his first two at-bats on a single and a walk. But he struck out with the bases loaded in the fourth inning against right-hander David Morgan.
“He looked good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Ohtani. “At-bat quality was good. There wasn’t any chase. I thought he hit the ball hard in his first at-bat, just missed a homer (in the seventh inning), took a walk. It was good. It’s been a while since he’s played in a game, but it felt like he wasn’t sped up at all.”
Ohtani hit out of the No. 2 spot in the lineup against left-hander Robbie Ray, while Mookie Betts remained the leadoff hitter for the fifth consecutive game. Ohtani is expected to play again Thursday and might return to the leadoff spot against Pivetta.
Glasnow is 2-1 with a 4.50 ERA in five starts since returning from a back injury. In his most recent outing Friday against the San Francisco Giants, he had a season-high 10 strikeouts in earning an 8-2 win.
In eight career appearances against San Diego (five starts), Glasnow is 0-1 with a 3.27 ERA.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
It was a win-or-go-home game for the Comets, and they live to fight another day after dominating the Aviators in Game 2 of the Championship Series in a 7-2 victory.
Player of the Day
While Zach Ehrhard and James Tibbs III led the way with the bat, it was Landon Knack’s outstanding work as a starter that allowed the Comets to open a five-run lead before the Aviators could think about entering the game. Doing a complete 180 from the previous game’s pitching struggles, Landon Knack didn’t walk anyone and struck out eight in 6.1 one-run innings.
For anyone closely monitoring Knack’s September stats, this was hardly a surprising development, considering he had come into the game with 11.2 scoreless innings this month, 7.2 of them in Triple-A with the Comets.
Triple-A Oklahoma City
The middle-infield combo of Noah Miller and Hyeseong Kim reached in front of Zach Ehrhard in the third inning, and the Comets’ leadoff hitter drove them both in to give his team a lead they would maintain until the end.
Between the third and fifth innings, the Comets scored six of their eventual seven runs, all unanswered, capped by a James Tibbs III three-run bomb, doing what he has done basically the whole year.
The Comets showed discipline to put the ball in play, ending the game with only five strikeouts, under half the total of the Aviators’ lineup. Ryan Fitzgerald, the veteran who was the only Comet to strike out multiple times, got on the scoreboard with a solo shot in the eighth.
Not only dominant, but Knack also found a way to be extremely efficient and could’ve easily gone further than the 6.1 innings he covered, getting the hook when he was at just 81 pitches. Recently demoted flamethrower Seth Halvorsen contributed a scoreless frame with a walk and two strikeouts. The Aviators’ second and final run came against Paul Gervase in the ninth inning.
Transactions
The Comets placed outfielder Chris Newell and pitcher Jackson Ferris on the Development List. The Dodgers optioned pitcher Kyle Hurt and outfielder Josue De Paula to the Comets. Lastly, they activated Emmet Sheehan as well.
Wednesday’s scores
- Las Vegas 2, Oklahoma City 7
Thursday’s schedule
- 7:05 p.m. PT: Oklahoma City (Cole Irvin) at Las Vegas (TBD)

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres moved to the brink of their third consecutive playoff appearance with a 5-1 road victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday.
Fernando Tatis Jr. had three hits as the Padres reduced their magic number for clinching a National League wild-card spot to one. San Diego sits in the top NL wild-card position, one game ahead of both the Chicago Cubs and the Philadelphia Phillies.
San Diego won for the 14th time in its past 16 games while coming out on top for just the fourth time in 12 games against Los Angeles this season. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
In his return to the roster after recovering from knee and biceps injuries, Shohei Ohtani went 1-for-4 with a walk as the Dodgers saw their 11-game home winning streak end. Andy Pages and Teoscar Hernandez each had three hits while Los Angeles ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9) gave up four runs (two earned) on five hits over six innings.
Brewers 4, Phillies 1
Brice Turang and Christian Yelich hit early home runs as visiting Milwaukee topped Philadelphia.
William Contreras knocked in two runs for the Brewers, who extended their franchise-record win total. Milwaukee needs to capture one of its final four games to reach 100 victories for the first time in team history. Logan Henderson (11-3) allowed one run in five innings.
Philadelphia starter Aaron Nola (7-11) permitted four runs and four hits in six innings. Bryson Stott doubled twice for the Phillies, who have a magic number of two to clinch a playoff berth.
Marlins 3, Cubs 2
Esteury Ruiz's hustle enabled visiting Miami to score the go-ahead run in the seventh inning, leading to a win over Chicago.
After a video review, Ruiz was declared safe at second base on what was originally ruled an inning-ending double play, with Agustin Ramirez scoring to break a 2-2 tie. Cade Gibson (6-2) threw one perfect inning, and ace Sandy Alcantara recorded his second save.
Cubs starter Kevin Gausman allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings, exiting after hurting his left shoulder while diving to make a tag at third base. Dansby Swanson hit a two-run single in the bottom of the sixth after Kyle Stowers socked a two-run homer in the top of the frame.
Diamondbacks 5, Rockies 3
Tim Tawa homered, Gabriel Moreno had three hits and Arizona continued its drive for a postseason berth with a win over Colorado in Denver.
The Diamondbacks have won four straight to move within three games of the Phillies and the Cubs in the chase for the last two NL wild-card positions with four games to play. Arizona starter Merrill Kelly (10-14) allowed two runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings.
Ezequiel Tovar homered and finished with two hits for the Rockies, who lost for the 14th time in 16 games. Rookie Mason Adams (0-2) struck out a career-high eight over a career-best six innings. He yielded four runs, all unearned, on five hits.
Mariners 6, Astros 5 (10 innings)
Josh Naylor lined a one-out single to center field with the bases loaded in the bottom of the 10th inning to score the deciding run as Seattle kept its slim playoff hopes alive with a victory against visiting Houston.
Dominic Canzone drove in three runs for the Mariners, whose only chance to make the postseason is to finish in a three-way tie with Houston and Texas, who are tied atop the American League West. Julio Rodriguez's bases-loaded walk tied the game before Naylor's winning hit.
Yainer Diaz hit a tiebreaking triple in the top of the 10th inning after earlier belting a two-run homer for the Astros. Houston closer Josh Hader (4-2) took the loss.
Mets 7, Rangers 2
Marcus Semien damaged his former team's playoff hopes when he hit a tiebreaking solo homer in the eighth inning to help New York prevail in Arlington, Texas.
Juan Soto socked a two-run homer in the third and Brett Baty added insurance with a pinch-hit grand slam in the ninth for the Mets. New York starter Nolan McLean (12-10) gave up two runs in seven innings.
The Rangers managed just four hits while losing their third game in a row. Jacob Latz (3-4) served up Semien's homer.
Red Sox 1, Guardians 0
Andruw Monasterio's sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray's six shutout innings propelled Boston past visiting Cleveland.
The Red Sox managed the lone run on 12 hits, all singles. They went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left eight men on base through five innings before Monasterio's run-scoring single broke the deadlock. Gray (18-5), who allowed four hits, increased his AL-leading win total.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) worked six frames, allowing one run on 10 hits. The Guardians remained tied with the White Sox atop the AL Central.
Royals 5, White Sox 4
Maikel Garcia's tiebreaking double in the seventh inning capped a three-hit, three-RBI night as Kansas City beat visiting Chicago.
While the Royals snapped a five-game skid, the White Sox missed a chance to regain control of the AL Central and clinch a playoff berth.
Connor Thomas (2-1) tossed two shutout innings for the win, and Steven Cruz recorded his eighth save. Kansas City's Carter Jensen and Chicago's Braden Montgomery each had three hits and a run.
Braves 3, Reds 2 (10 innings)
Mauricio Dubon's infield chopper to the mound in the 10th inning gave host Atlanta a walk-off victory over Cincinnati.
Braves starter Chris Sale pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed one run while striking out 10, reaching 200 strikeouts for the ninth time in his career. Matt Olson and Austin Riley homered for Atlanta, and Brent Suter (3-2) tossed a perfect top of the 10th.
Juan Brito led off the game with a home run, and he and Matt McLain each had two hits for the Reds. Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott fired a season-high seven innings and allowed two runs.
Orioles 4, Blue Jays 2 (Game 1)
Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated visiting Toronto from playoff contention by winning in the first game of a doubleheader.
The Blue Jays were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series.
Chris Bassitt (9-5) pitched five-plus innings to notch a victory in his third consecutive start. He gave up two runs on seven hits. Max Scherzer (3-9) surrendered four runs and four hits in five innings.
Orioles 4, Blue Jays 2 (Game 2)
Christian Encarnacion-Strand homered and drove in three runs and Trey Gibson took a shutout into the seventh inning as Baltimore completed a doubleheader sweep of visiting Toronto to stay in playoff contention.
Baltimore must win its remaining three games and have the White Sox lose their remaining four in order to have a chance for an AL wild-card spot. Gibson (2-3), a rookie who hadn't pitched in the major leagues since June 30, gave up three hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Davis Schneider hit a two-run ninth-inning homer off Felix Bautista in the nightcap for the Blue Jays. Toronto rookie starter CJ Van Eyk (0-2) allowed four runs on four hits in five innings.
Yankees 9, Rays 2
Ryan McMahon hit a third-inning grand slam and tied a career high with five RBIs while Ben Rice hit a pair of solo homers as host New York rolled past Tampa Bay.
McMahon drove in five runs for the fourth time in his career. Rice homered on the first pitch of the contest to become the 13th Yankee with 40 homers in a season. He later hit his 41st. Gerrit Cole (10-9) allowed two runs on three hits in 5 2/3 innings.
Jonny DeLuca hit an RBI double and Cedric Mullins homered for the Rays. Mason Englert (0-4) allowed eight runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings.
Nationals 4, Tigers 2
Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer and visiting Washington held on for a victory over Detroit as the Nationals won the three-game series 2-1.
Brady House had two hits and scored a run while CJ Abrams, who homered twice on Tuesday, reached base three times and knocked in a run for Washington. Will Dion (2-2) tossed two innings of one-run relief, and Yovanny Cruz got four outs for his first career save.
Detroit starter Framber Valdez (10-12) gave up two runs and four hits over 5 1/3 innings. Ben Malgeri homered and drove in both of the Tigers' runs, and Kevin McGonigle added three hits.
Twins 4, Giants 2
Pinch hitter Walker Jenkins broke a seventh-inning tie with an RBI single as Minnesota completed a 4-3 road trip with a win over San Francisco.
Luke Keaschall drove in two runs with a homer and a sacrifice fly while Josh Bell added an RBI single for the Twins. Yoendrys Gomez (3-4) threw 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief, and Andrew Morris escaped a ninth-inning jam for his fifth save.
Shay Whitcomb had two hits for the Giants, who have lost five out of six. Reliever Dylan Smith (0-6) yielded two runs while getting just two outs.
Cardinals 5, Pirates 1
Matthew Liberatore struck out six over 5 2/3 innings and JJ Wetherholt had three hits and an RBI to lead St. Louis to a victory at Pittsburgh.
Liberatore (6-14) allowed only one run -- on a solo homer by Brandon Lowe -- as the Cardinals snapped the Pirates' season-high-tying five-game winning streak. St. Louis' Jose Fermin went 2-for-4.
Lowe had two hits and Ryan O'Hearn added two doubles for Pittsburgh. Pirates reliever Brandon Eisert (3-3) gave up three runs in two-thirds of an inning.
Athletics 7, Angels 3
Rookie Henry Bolte recorded the first four-hit game of his career and Donovan Walton hit a three-run homer to help the Athletics top Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
Shea Langeliers had a two-run double and Bolte scored twice, had two doubles and drove in one run for the A's, who assured they will avoid a 100-loss season. Geoff Hartlieb (2-1) threw 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief.
Mike Trout and Vaughn Grissom homered for the Angels, who are two losses shy of the first 100-loss season in franchise history. Walbert Urena (9-11) allowed five runs and seven hits over four innings.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Roki Sasaki's request for change of plans shows he's in right mindset ahead of Dodgers playoff run
item.dc:creator: Evan Roberts
item.description: With the regular season winding down, the Los Angeles Dodgers have used bullpen days the last two games against the San Diego Padres and San Francisco Giants. Yoshinobu Yamamoto was originally the probable starter for Tuesday's game against San Diego, but the Dodgers are planning out a schedule to manage Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, while also planning out their playoff rotation. The back-up plan was to open with Roki Sasaki, who had missed almost a month due to a blist
item.content:encoded:
With the regular season winding down, the Los Angeles Dodgers have used bullpen days the last two games against the San Diego Padres and San Francisco Giants.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto was originally the probable starter for Tuesday's game against San Diego, but the Dodgers are planning out a schedule to manage Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, while also planning out their playoff rotation.
The back-up plan was to open with Roki Sasaki, who had missed almost a month due to a blister, but the youngster essentially re-wrote the lineup card.
“I said I wanted to pitch out of the bullpen,” Sasaki said per Dylan Hernandez of the New York Post. Rather than starting the game, Sasaki was inserted after a one inning each from Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski and Blake Treinen.
The 24-year-old righty pitched a scoreless fourth inning, and struck out two, but did allow two hits in his first outing since August 26th. It was Sasaki's first relief appearance since Game 6 of the World Series last year.
Dodgers' test run with Roki Sasaki was a success
Sasaki is clearly a prideful guy who wants to carve out a career as a starting pitcher. He was not thrilled about the move to the bullpen last season. Unlike many of his teammates, Sasaki isn't signed to a monster contract and likely wants to continue to start games in order to bank a large extension or free agency contract down the road. However, he's clearly in the right state of mind at the moment...perhaps unlike the Dodgers?
It's a little strange that the Dodgers were not planning to deploy Sasaki in relief of this game originally, right? He hadn't come out of the bullpen all season, and baseball players are as routine-oriented as human beings come. It's a little strange, but Sasaki clearly is locked in heading into October.
Sasaki appeared in nine postseason games last year. Sasaki has now appeared in 12 career games as a reliever including both the regular season and postseason, and the Dodgers are 12-0 in those games.
Sasaki has has a 0.66 ERA, 12:5 K:BB, and three saves in just over 13 innings of relief. The hopes are that a rejuvenated and healthy Sasaki can give this shaky, injury-riddled bullpen some stability before a possible three-peat.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Hyeseong Kim Makes His Case for Dodgers' Postseason Roster
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Utility player Hyeseong Kim is giving the Los Angeles Dodgers something to think about as they’re putting together the postseason roster. Kim, who’s been with the Oklahoma City Comets since May, went 2-for-4 in Game 2 of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series Wednesday night. Kim’s night also included a double, an RBI and a run scored in the Comets’ 7-1 win over the Las Vegas Aviators, a victory that forces a deciding Game 3 on Thursday. It came on the heels of another 2-for-4 game for Kim
item.content:encoded:
Utility player Hyeseong Kim is giving the Los Angeles Dodgers something to think about as they’re putting together the postseason roster.
Kim, who’s been with the Oklahoma City Comets since May, went 2-for-4 in Game 2 of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series Wednesday night.
Kim’s night also included a double, an RBI and a run scored in the Comets’ 7-1 win over the Las Vegas Aviators, a victory that forces a deciding Game 3 on Thursday.
It came on the heels of another 2-for-4 game for Kim on Tuesday night in which he also scored two runs, a sign of progress amid a largely uneven season at the plate.
How has Hyeseong Kim played in 2026?
Kim’s production at the major-league and minor-league levels has been virtually identical in 2026, and not in a way that shows Kim living up to his potential.
In the majors, he hit .259 with one home run and 11 RBIs.
In the minors, where he’s spent about triple the time, he is hitting .262 with three homers and 31 RBIs.
He has also stolen five bases in the majors and 15 in the minors.
While the production hasn’t necessarily been eye-popping, his skills could be a huge boon to the Dodgers in the playoffs, something manager Dave Roberts addressed recently.
What do the Dodgers plan to do with Hyeseong Kim?
Roberts said that the Dodgers plan to use next week, when they are almost assuredly going to get a bye for the wild card round, to meet with Kim and possibly add him to the postseason roster.
“My expectation is that Kim will be here during the off week and potentially be in the conversation for the postseason, because he has the ability to run and play defense and steal a base,” he said.
That said, those offensive numbers that Kim has put up in Triple-A and the majors this season give Roberts and the Dodgers coaches and executives pause, he said.
“I think for Hyeseong, it’s the at bat consistency,” Roberts said. “I don’t think that his offense has been consistent.”
Especially compared to some of the other players who are fighting for a playoff roster spot, Kim’s relative inconsistency could spell doom for his postseason hopes.
“For us, the at bat quality, for example, that Alex Freeland is giving us has been very good,” Roberts said. “He gets on base. I think for Hyeseong, just trying to find something consistent and perform consistently. And to be quite frank, he just hasn’t been as consistent as he can be. But if he can get more consistent with the bat, then he can be a big piece.”
Dodgers fans will find out in the coming days if Kim has indeed done enough to earn a spot for October, but his supporters can rest assured that he’s putting his best foot forward in these Triple-A playoffs.

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodgers notes: Postseason bullpen in a good spot
item.dc:creator: Andy Lane Chapman
item.description: Tuesday night’s game against the San Diego Padres was reminiscent of the 2024 playoffs when the Dodgers were forced to employ a bullpen in the NLDS to keep their playoff hopes alive against those same Padres. Both outcomes were the same, with the bullpen shutting down the Friars and getting a big win. That postseason saw a lot of bullpen usage, and in this one the Dodgers are stacked with starters. Still, the bullpen is always a big part of the postseason. As Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic points
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday night’s game against the San Diego Padres was reminiscent of the 2024 playoffs when the Dodgers were forced to employ a bullpen in the NLDS to keep their playoff hopes alive against those same Padres. Both outcomes were the same, with the bullpen shutting down the Friars and getting a big win.
That postseason saw a lot of bullpen usage, and in this one the Dodgers are stacked with starters. Still, the bullpen is always a big part of the postseason.
As Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic points out, 41 days ago manager Dave Roberts was asking the media what choices did he truly have to deploy in the ninth inning of games. Now, he could have several options.
Edwin Diaz, the closer they paid handsomely in the offseason, has not had a great season. He’s been on the IL twice and had an era over 11.00 at one point this summer. But since returning from his latest IL stint, he has faced 11 batters, struck out six and only allowed two to reach base.
“I think it’s one of those things where if you’re one of the 12 pitchers on a postseason roster, you’re in the trust tree,” Roberts said “He’s put himself right smack in that conversation. Given all that he’s had to go through this year to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
Roki Sasaki is also someone who will be in the mix for the ninth inning spot. He has also just returned from his own IL stint, pitching with dermabond on his blister. He allowed two singles, but worked around them for a scoreless inning in Tuesday night’s game. He will appear in Friday night’s game as he continues to work towards a spot in the bullpen that will likely vary as the postseason goes on.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ most reliable arm out of the bullpen this season, and Roberts has remarked how it would be nice to be able to use Scott in high leverage spots that may not come just in the ninth inning.
“I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there,” Roberts said. “You just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.”
Roberts also added that the team is sitting in their best position with regards to the bullpen as they have ever been. Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart round out the current options, and the team hopes that Edguardo Henriquez can recover from his back issues to appear in the playoffs. With the starters this team has overall this may be the best pitching staff the Dodgers have ever sent to the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
レギュラーシーズンが最終盤を迎えたMLBは、残り4日という状況でプレーオフ行きのチケットはまだ6枠が残されており、ポストシーズン進出争いに絡むチームの試合は、熱を増すばかりである。
そんな中、『MLB.com』は「2026年シーズンを象徴する驚異的なスタッツ」と題した記事を掲載し、様々な数字から今季を振り返っている。
記事ではシカゴ・カブスのピート・クロウ＝アームストロングが、シーズンの1/3を消化した時点でのOPS『.673』を挙げている。現地9月22日の試合を終えた時点でのOPSは.950まで上がっており、いかに彼がシーズン中盤以降に驚異的な巻き返しを見せたかを示した。
また、3シーズン連続で100敗以上を喫した翌シーズンのチームとして歴代最多となった、シカゴ・ホワイトソックスの『81勝』（これまでは70勝が最多）といった数字も紹介された。
さらに記事ではロサンゼルス・ドジャースの大谷 翔平の『235』という数字にも着目しており、「これはショウヘイ・オオタニが85回2/3を投げて記録したERA+である」と説明。
ERA+とは該当選手の所属リーグの平均やパークファクター（球場の投打の有利・不利を表す指数）を加味した防御率の調整値であり、100をリーグ平均とし、それより高ければ高いほど優秀と見なされる。
続けて記事では、「ケガの影響で7月初旬に投手としての公式戦登板を中断せざるを得なかったことを踏まえると、オオタニの活躍を当たり前のことと捉えたり、その二刀流シーズンを軽く見てしまったりしがちだ」と前置きした。
その上で、「しかし、これは決して普通のことではない！」と断言し、「近代野球において、85イニング以上を投げ、かつこれと同等以上のERA+を記録したアメリカン・リーグおよびナショナル・リーグの先発投手は、オオタニ以外にわずか8例しか存在しないのである」と、その理由を説明。
さらに記事では、「もちろん、シーズンを通して投げ抜いた上でこれほどのERA+を記録する方が、より素晴らしい偉業であることは言うまでもない」としつつ、「しかし、もう1つ驚くべき点があるのをご存知だろうか？」とした。

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodgers 11-game home winning streak snapped in 5-1 loss to Padres
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky
item.description: After shutting out the Padres on Tuesday, the Dodgers could only muster one run in a 5-1 defeat on Wednesday, snapping their home winning streak at 11 games. Dodgers 11-game home winning streak snapped in 5-1 loss to Padres Yoshinobu Yamamoto tallies six innings but gets one run of support, Manny Machado’s home run makes the difference. Both Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray kept the hitters in check over their first three innings, as Yamamoto secured three shutout innings on just 36 pitches whi
item.content:encoded:
After shutting out the Padres on Tuesday, the Dodgers could only muster one run in a 5-1 defeat on Wednesday, snapping their home winning streak at 11 games.
Dodgers 11-game home winning streak snapped in 5-1 loss to Padres
Yoshinobu Yamamoto tallies six innings but gets one run of support, Manny Machado’s home run makes the difference.
Both Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray kept the hitters in check over their first three innings, as Yamamoto secured three shutout innings on just 36 pitches while Ray needed 70 pitches in that same time.
Yamamoto began the top of the fourth inning by brushing the jersey of Dustin Harris on an inside pitch to give San Diego a leadoff baserunner, and Manny Machado ensured the Padres wouldn’t be shut out again as he launched a two-run home run to center field to give San Diego the first lead.
The Dodgers responded with two consecutive singles from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker to begin the bottom of the fourth inning, and Andy Pages had his first hit back from the injured list with a bloop single to center field. Ray managed to get Max Muncy to fly out to shallow center, but his night was done after tossing 84 pitches over 3 1/3 innings. He was charged with a run as Tommy Edman lifted a sacrifice fly to put the Dodgers on the board. Mookie Betts walked on four pitches to make it bases loaded with two outs for Shohei Ohtani, but David Morgan got him whiffing on a fastball at 99 miles per hour on a 3-2 count to leave them loaded.
San Diego picked up where they left off against Yamamoto in the top of the fifth inning, as Ethan Salas and Fernando Tatis Jr. both singled to open the frame. A bunt attempt from Harris was hit right back to Yamamoto, but an errant throw to third allowed Salas to score. Manny Machado brought home Tatis with a sacrifice fly to center field, giving him three RBI on the night and making it a three-run San Diego lead.
Yamamoto would finish his night going six innings, marking the first time he didn’t log at least seven innings in the month of September. Wednesday’s outing was the first time since September 2 where Yamamoto allowed at least two earned runs, with his four strikeouts on the night being the fewest since he struck out three against the Boston Red Sox on August 1. Yamamoto ends the regular season with a 2.53 ERA, striking out 182 hitters across 185 innings.
The Dodger bullpen would hold San Diego in check until the top of the ninth inning as Blake Treinen allowed an RBI single to Freddy Fermin, allowing Samad Taylor to score to make it a 5-1 Padres lead.
Teoscar Hernández recorded another three-hit game, his third of the month, finishing 3-4 with three singles while raising his season average to .270 for the first time since June 30.
Andy Pages also finished with a three-hit night in his second game off the injured list, giving him his first multi-hit game since August 17 against the Colorado Rockies. Shohei Ohtani finished 1-4 with a single, a walk and two strikeouts in his first game off the injured list.
With the Dodgers losing on Wednesday, they once again sit two games back of the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League playoff picture. The Dodgers are still four games above the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye, and their magic number to secure a bye remains at 1.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Manny Machado (29)
- WP— Yuki Matsui (4-1): 1 IP, 1 hit, 0 runs, 1 walk, 0 strikeouts
- LP— Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9): 6 IP, 5 hits, 4 runs (2 earned runs), 1 walk, 4 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers play their final home game of the regular season against San Diego on Thursday (7:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before heading up to San Francisco for their final regular season series. Tyler Glasnow faces Nick Pivetta.

item.content:encoded:
Padres down Dodgers, grab solo lead in NL wild-card standings
(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres moved to the brink of their third consecutive playoff appearance with a 5-1 road victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday.
Fernando Tatis Jr. had three hits as the Padres (88-70) reduced their magic number for clinching a National League wild-card spot to one. San Diego sits in the top NL wild-card position, one game ahead of both the Chicago Cubs (87-71) and the Philadelphia Phillies (87-71).
Five San Diego relievers combined for 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Bradgley Rodriguez (4-3) fanned three in two innings.
San Diego won for the 14th time in its past 16 games while coming out on top for just the fourth time in 12 games against Los Angeles this season. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
In his return to the active roster after recovering from knee and biceps injuries, Shohei Ohtani went 1-for-4 with a walk as the Dodgers (97-61) saw their 11-game home winning streak end. Ohtani struck out with the bases loaded to end the fourth inning and flied out to the wall in center field in the seventh.
Andy Pages and Teoscar Hernandez each had three hits while Los Angeles ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9) gave up four runs (two earned) on five hits over six innings but was burned by his own throwing error. Yamamoto fanned four and walked one.
Machado gave the Padres a 2-0 lead in the fourth when he crushed a first-pitch sinker from Yamamoto over the center field wall for his 29th home run of the season.
The Dodgers loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the fourth. Robbie Ray got Max Muncy to fly out, then was replaced by David Morgan after 3 1/3 innings. Morgan gave up a sacrifice fly to Edman, cutting the Padres' lead to 2-1, before striking out Ohtani.
Ohtani appeared to walk on a 3-1 pitch, but Padres catcher Ethan Salas successfully challenged the pitch. Morgan eventually got Ohtani swinging at a 3-2 sinker.
The Padres made it 3-1 in the fifth when Yamamoto was off target on a throw to third base following a bunt from Dustin Harris with runners on first and second. Salas scored on the play, and Machado followed with a sacrifice fly to right-center for a 4-1 lead.
San Diego added a run in the ninth. Samad Taylor walked, stole second and third and came home on a single from Freddy Fermin.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [nbclosangeles.com] Ohtani returns to Dodgers lineup and delivers hit in first at-bat
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort. He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed. “I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.” A roar went up from Dodger fans as
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani got a hit in his return to the Los Angeles Dodgers' lineup on Wednesday night after missing two weeks with right biceps discomfort.
He batted second as the designated hitter against the San Diego Padres and left-handed starter Robbie Ray. Ohtani hits left-handed and throws and pitches right-handed.
“I’m not expecting too much,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s been a while since he’s played, but it’s just good to get him in there.”
A roar went up from Dodger fans as Ohtani walked to the plate to Michael Bublé's “Feeling Good.” He promptly lined a 2-1 pitch from Ray into right field and the fans got loud again. Ohtani was out at second base when Will Smith grounded into a fielder's choice to third.
Mookie Betts was in Ohtani's usual leadoff spot, where he's been since the two-way superstar went on the injured list on Sept. 8.
Betts is hitting .366 with six home runs, 21 RBIs, 13 walks and 18 runs scored in 18 games in September. He's tied for third in the major leagues with 26 hits this month, and also ranks among National League leaders this month in extra-base hits, RBIs, total bases, doubles and runs.
Ohtani last played on Sept. 7 against Cincinnati and came in hitting .277 with 30 homers, 80 RBIs, 89 runs scored and 80 walks in 134 games. He appeared physically compromised at the plate, shaking out his arm and wincing at times.
Local
Get Los Angeles's latest local news on crime, entertainment, weather, schools, cost of living and more. Here's your go-to source for today's LA news.
“A few weeks ago you could see that he couldn’t hit a fastball, he was underneath everything and it was a slower swing,” Roberts said. “Just controlling the swing, the barrel, I think that’s something I’ll look at and obviously stuff like the wincing, but I don’t expect to see any of that.”
Roberts said he likely would have Ohtani leading off and Betts hitting second against right-handed pitching.
The Dodgers conclude their three-game set against the Padres on Thursday, then head to San Francisco for three games against the Giants to end the regular season.
Roberts expects to see a focused Ohtani at the plate.
“It’s go-time for all of us and I think he’s in a good spot,” Roberts said. “He's getting ready for the postseason. His mind should be there and my bet is that that’s where it’s at.”
In other moves, pitcher Tarik Skubal was reinstated from the bereavement list. He is scheduled to start Friday at San Francisco. Reliever Kyle Hurt was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Rookie Josue De Paula sent back to minors, could return for postseason
With Ohtani's return, Josue De Paula was sent down to Triple-A to join the Comets in the Pacific Coast League playoffs against the Las Vegas Aviators. De Paula had been in the lineup as the DH.
De Paula quickly became a fan favorite during Ohtani's absence. The 21-year-old New York native reached base safely in 10 of his first 11 games in the majors. He went 2 for 3 with a run scored and a walk while notching his first career triple in the Dodgers' 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday.
“He performed more than admirably,” Roberts said. “This also just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him.”
If De Paula makes the postseason roster, he would serve as a pinch-hitter.
“Josue has been awesome,” said Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations. “Injected some real life and energy into our team.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Por primera vez en toda la temporada, los Dodgers presentaron exactamente el lineup de nueve jugadores que habían imaginado al armar su roster. Pero con Shohei Ohtani de regreso de la lista de lesionados la noche del miércoles, en una derrota por 5-1 ante los Padres de San Diego, el principal objetivo no era alcanzar la perfección de inmediato, sino establecer una base sólida de cara a octubre.
Activado antes del juego del miércoles tras pasar 15 días en la lista de lesionados debido a persistentes molestias en el bíceps derecho y dolor en la rodilla izquierda, Ohtani retomó su puesto como bateador designado. Como segundo bate por primera vez este año, dio una chispa temprana con un sencillo al jardín derecho en su primera aparición en el plato y luego negoció un boleto en el tercer inning.
Ohtani terminó la noche de 4-1 con dos ponches. Su oportunidad más importante llegó en la parte baja del cuarto episodio, con los Dodgers abajo por dos carreras. Con las bases llenas y dos outs, Ohtani llevó la cuenta al máximo ante el relevista de los Padres David Morgan, pero se ponchó tirándole al lanzamiento decisivo, apagando la mejor amenaza de los Dodgers en toda la noche.
A pesar del ponche en una situación de alta presión, las primeras señales le dieron a los Dodgers el indicador que más necesitaban: Ohtani está saludable.
A diferencia de principios de septiembre, cuando sus gestos de dolor y un swing limitado encendieron las alarmas, Ohtani hizo sus swings con total intención y se movió sin molestias.
"Sin duda se siente mucho mejor después del descanso", dijo antes del juego Andrew Friedman, presidente de operaciones de béisbol de los Dodgers. "Lo más importante es conseguirle la mayor cantidad de turnos al bate posible, para que recupere ritmo y timing. Ahora, si serán los cinco juegos o cuatro de cinco, lo iremos determinando según la carga de trabajo y cómo se sienta. Creo que conseguir la mayor cantidad de turnos posible y recuperar ese ritmo y timing antes de entrar en octubre será de mucha ayuda. Pero lo más importante es cuánto mejor se siente".

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani gets a hit in his return, but Dodgers fall to the Padres
Shohei Ohtani’s swing was a little out in front of a slider delivered by Padres left-hander Robbie Ray. But Ohtani held back his hands long enough to extend them to the pitch and shoot it through the right side of the infield.
It wasn’t flashy. But considering it was his first at-bat in over two weeks, in a tough matchup no less, it was a promising sign.
The good news quickly dried up for the Dodgers after that, as they fell to the Padres 5-1, missing a chance to clinch a first-round bye with a win. But Ohtani’s return was still significant, and the success of his end-of-season tune-up will have playoff implications.
The Dodgers activated Ohtani, who went one-for-four Wednesday, from the 15-day IL before the game and optioned rookie Josue De Paula to Triple-A. De Paula is still under consideration for the National League Division Series roster as a bat of the bench.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” manager Dave Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
It was Josue De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the IL. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot.
De Paula joined triple-A Oklahoma City for Game 2 of the PCL Championship on Wednesday. And Ohtani slid into the Dodgers lineup, hitting second in the batting order for the first time this season, with Mookie Betts leading off against the Padres southpaw.
“I know Shohei, Mookie, they’re always on board with whatever I decide to do,” Roberts said. “I think it just makes it tougher to navigate versus left. There’s a Mookie tax [to get to Ohtani]. If you want to get to Freddie [Freeman], there’s a Will Smith tax. I like that. And versus a right hander I like kind of flipping those two for the same reasons.”
Ohtani, welcomed back in his first at-bat by a partial standing ovation, walked in his second plate appearance. And with two out and the bases loaded in the bottom of the fourth inning, he appeared to have walked again.
Then Padres catcher Ethan Salas tapped the top of his head to challenge the ball call. And an ABS review showed the fastball had clipped the top of the strike zone. Ohtani fouled off the next two pitches before whiffing on a sinker to end the inning.
That missed opportunity rolled right into a sloppy fifth inning for the Dodgers defense.
Starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto had given up a two-run homer to Manny Machado the previous inning but had otherwise avoided damage.
To open the fifth, he induced Salas to hit the ball on the ground, but it got away from second baseman Tommy Edman as he dove up the middle, for a single.
Yamamoto then got a soft grounder out of Fernando Tatís Jr. But it was too soft, giving Tatís time to reach first before third baseman Max Muncy could get off a throw.
With runners on first and second, Yamamoto had a chance to contribute on defense, fielding Dustin Harris’ comebacker bunt. But Yamamoto’s throw to third sailed wide, allowing a run to score. Machado then made it a 4-1 game with a sacrifice fly.
Ohtani came up to the plate again in the seventh inning and put Dodgers fans on the edge of their seats by sending a long fly ball to straightaway center field. But the cheers died down as it fell shy well short of the 395-foot wall.
The top of the Dodgers order got one last chance to start a rally in the ninth inning, against star closer Mason Miller. Only Will Smith reached base, on a walk, and advanced to third on defensive indifference. Ohtani struck out on a slider.
“[Ohtani] certainly feels way better with the rest,” president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said before the game. “The biggest thing with five games to go is get him as many at-bats as we can, some rhythm and timing.”
Ohtani could get a day off in that span, Friedman said, but the Dodgers will make those decisions based on how he’s feeling.
After defeating the Padres, the Dodgers have five games left to round into playoff form. They get a big piece, Shohei Ohtani, back Wednesday.
“Just getting as many at-bats as he can and that rhythm and timing back before we head into October is going to be really helpful,” Friedman said.
Ohtani was not in rhythm before he landed on the IL. In the last three weeks before the Dodgers finally shelved him, he had a .130 batting average. And he only had two hits in his last seven games (26 at-bats) before the move.
“You end up making subconscious adjustments where you’re protecting yourself,” Friedman said, “and there’s just slight degradation as that’s happening that compounds over time.”

item.content:encoded:
また“不在”の山本由伸 登板1時間前にまさかの1枚…大谷イジリも話題、集合写真に空白
球団公式Xが投稿「Your 2026 Los Angeles Dodgers.」
【MLB】ドジャース ー パドレス（日本時間24日・ロサンゼルス）
ドジャースは23日（日本時間24日）、本拠地でのパドレス戦に臨む。試合前には球団公式SNSが更新され、「チーム・フォト」の様子が公開された。負傷者リストから復帰を果たした大谷翔平投手や佐々木朗希投手が笑顔を見せるなか、“エース”の姿はなかった。
球団公式X（旧ツイッター）は試合開始の約1時間前、「Your 2026 Los Angeles Dodgers.」として選手とコーチ陣の集合写真をアップした。デーブ・ロバーツ監督らコーチ陣は1列目、選手たちは2～3列目でカメラに写った。大谷は指揮官のちょうど上で、ほぼ写真のセンターにいる。
写真の左にはフレディ・フリーマン内野手、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手が並ぶなか、ベッツの横に不自然な“空白”があった。チーム・フォト全体を見渡すと、山本由伸投手の姿はどこにも見られなかった。山本はこの日先発登板することもあり、参加しなかったと思われる。
山本といえば、メジャー2年目の昨季に初めてオールスターに選ばれたものの、ホテルに一度戻った際に写真撮影が行われて“不在”となり、大谷からもイジられたことが話題を呼んだ。

item.content:encoded:
ドジャースの山本由伸投手は23日（日本時間24日）、本拠地でのパドレス戦に今季28試合目の先発登板。6回88球を投げて5安打4失点（自責点2）1四球4奪三振。今季9敗目を喫した。
自身の悪送球でリードを広げられる場面も見られたが、メジャー単独トップとなる今季22度目のクオリティスタートを記録した。
■レギュラーシーズン最終登板
山本は初回、先頭のフェルナンド・タティスJr.外野手に二塁への内野安打を許したものの、続くダスティン・ハリス外野手を二ゴロ、マニー・マチャド内野手を中飛、タイ・フランス内野手を左直に仕留めて無失点の立ち上がりを見せた。
2回表と3回表は三者凡退の好投。4回表、マチャドに中堅への29号2ランを被弾し先制を許すと、5回表には、イーサン・サラス捕手とタティスJr.の連打で無死一、二塁のピンチ。続くハリスの投ゴロを三塁へ悪送球し、二塁走者が生還。犠飛でも追加点を奪われた。それでも後続を切って、6回表も三者凡退にまとめて降板した。
この日の山本は、6回88球を投げて5安打4失点（自責点2）1四球4奪三振。フォーシームが最速96.6マイル（約155.5キロ）を計測。全88球の内訳は、スプリット24、シンカー19、カットボール13、フォーシーム12、カーブ11、スライダー9だった。自身のミスが絡んだ4失点ながらも、自責点は2。今季22回目のクオリティスタートはメジャー単独トップとなっている。
山本はレギュラーシーズン最終登板を終えて、28先発、14勝9敗、防御率2.53、182奪三振。次戦はポストシーズンの地区シリーズ第1戦の先発が予定されている。

item.title: [sandiegouniontribune.com] Padres pregame: Jason Adam activated, Griffin Canning optioned ahead of Game 2 vs. Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Jeff Sanders
