23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy Diaz drove in four runs on a pair of singles.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left for New York. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Yankees 2, Rays 0 (Game 1)
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as host New York recorded a shutout over Tampa Bay in the opener of a day-night doubleheader.
With the victory, the Yankees temporarily prevented the Rays from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot.
New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rodon struck out eight in his 100th career win and also reached 1,500 strikeouts for his career. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9.
Dodgers 7, Padres 0
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and Los Angeles inched closer to the best record in the National League with a shutout of visiting San Diego.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the National League Division Series to one. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two.
Phillies 6, Brewers 4
Bryson Stott delivered the tiebreaking hit in the eighth inning to guide Philadelphia to a victory over visiting Milwaukee. Brandon Marsh homered and knocked in three runs as the Phillies lowered their magic number to two to clinch a postseason berth.
Zack Wheeler ended up with a no-decision after striking out 11 while giving up three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Wheeler struck out the first seven batters he faced, setting a Phillies record for consecutive strikeouts to begin a game. His first-inning strikeout of Brice Turang was the 2,000th of his career.
The Brewers saw their lead over the Dodgers for the top record in the majors shrink to one as they lost just the third time in their last 13 games. William Contreras knocked in three runs.
Marlins 8, Cubs 2 (12 innings)
Griffin Conine plated the go-ahead run that ignited a six-run 12th inning for visiting Miami, which snapped a three-game losing by beating Chicago and postponing the Cubs' playoff celebration for at least a day.
On a night when runs were scarce until the final inning, both teams endured a pair of scoreless extra frames before Conine broke the drought with a leadoff, golf-shot single off Caleb Thielbar that fell just inside the left field line. Esteury Ruiz, the automatic runner, scored from second to make it 3-2 as the Marlins sent 10 batters to the plate in the inning.
The Cubs could have clinched a wild-card playoff spot with a win or Arizona loss, but neither of those happened keeping the Diamondbacks mathematically alive. Josh Ekness (3-4) struck out a pair in the 11th inning to get the win while Thielbar (3-4) gave up three runs -- two earned -- in his inning of work.
Guardians 3, Red Sox 2
Nathaniel Lowe drove in Chase DeLauter with a sacrifice fly in the ninth inning and Cleveland held on to beat host Boston in the first game of a three-game series.
Cleveland not only extended its winning streak to six but maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the AL Central.
Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings, his 14th straight start allowing three runs or fewer. Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15.
White Sox 14, Royals 11
Chase Meidroth smacked a three-run home run among his three hits and drove in five, and Brenton Doyle, Randal Grichuk and Munetaka Murakami also homered to power Chicago past host Kansas City.
Chicago won for the fourth time in five games to remain one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox, who hold the third and final AL wild-card spot, reduced their magic number to earn a playoff berth to three.
Vinnie Pasquantino hit a ninth-inning grand slam for the Royals, who lost their fifth straight. He went 3-for-5 with a double and also drove in five.
Nationals 3, Tigers 1
CJ Abrams hit a pair of home runs and drove in all three runs as visiting Washington topped Detroit. Abrams reached 100 RBIs for the season with his solo shot in the second inning, then broke a 1-1 tie in the seventh with his 33rd long ball of the season, a two-run blast.
Dylan Crews had two hits and scored the other run for the Nationals. Rookie Jackson Kent (2-4) earned the win in long relief. He allowed one run on six hits over four innings and struck out three. Opener Riley Cornelio lasted 2 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking three.
Ben Malgeri scored the Tigers' only run. Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark each had two hits.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 0
Jared Jones and two relievers combined on a one-hitter as Pittsburgh beat visiting St. Louis for a fifth straight win. Jones (5-6) lowered his ERA to 1.08 in four September starts and struck out nine with zero walks over seven innings while throwing 63 of his 86 pitches for strikes.
Pittsburgh broke a scoreless tie with two outs in the sixth inning on Ryan O'Hearn's RBI single against Andre Pallante (12-8). Pallante allowed one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over six innings.
St. Louis struck out 14 times and lost for the fifth time in its last six games.
Astros 7, Mariners 0
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as Houston slugged and pitched its way past host Seattle.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros, who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the West. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings of relief.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle. The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Reds 4, Braves 0
Brandon Williamson fired six scoreless innings and Cincinnati supported him with three solo homers to defeat host Atlanta in the opener of a three-game series.
Cincinnati ended a two-game losing streak and evened the season series with Atlanta at 2-2. Williamson (5-4) worked six scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two strikeouts. Elly De La Cruz (29), Dane Myers (8) and Eugenio Suarez (25) each hit a home run for the Reds. It was Suarez's 350th career homer, making him the 10th active player to reach that mark.
Atlanta starter JR Ritchie (1-4) pitched five innings and allowed one run on four hits and three walks. The rookie struck out a career-high eight batters.
Mets 6, Rangers 3
Francisco Alvarez laced a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth, then scored an insurance run on an unusual sacrifice fly for visiting New York, who damaged Texas' playoff hopes with a win in the opener of a three-game interleague series in Arlington.
Juan Soto had an RBI single in the third, and Carson Benge capped the scoring with a run-scoring double in the seventh for the Mets. The club won hours after removing the interim tag from manager Andy Green and signing him to a three-year extension.
Josh Jung had an RBI double in the third, and Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford lofted sacrifice flies in the fourth for the Rangers, who entered Tuesday with a one-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West.
Diamondbacks 7, Rockies 2
Nolan Arenado homered and doubled among his three hits, Michael Soroka tossed seven strong innings, and Arizona kept its slim postseason hopes alive with a win over host Colorado in Denver.
Geraldo Perdomo also had three hits and Ildemaro Vargas finished with two hits for Arizona, which remains alive in the NL wild-card race, sitting four games behind Philadelphia, San Diego and the Chicago Cubs for the third and final spot with five games to go.
Mickey Moniak homered for Colorado, which finished with just three hits and just one after the third inning. The Rockies (57-100) are the first team to lose 100 or more games in four straight seasons since the 1962-65 New York Mets.
Twins 3, Giants 2
Walker Jenkins homered, Luke Keaschall contributed both offensively and defensively, and Minnesota evened its road interleague series against San Francisco.
Taj Bradley (12-6) combined with four relievers on a six-hitter for the Twins, who used two late diving catches by Keaschall in right field to prevent the Giants from taking the first two of the series.
Bradley allowed just one other hit -- a fifth-inning single by Drew Gilbert -- in his six innings. He walked three and struck out six. Keaschall's one-out triple scored Ryan Kreidler, then Brooks Lee gave Minnesota the lead for good with a run-scoring single to plate Keaschall.
A's 9, Angels 7
Carlos Cortes hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning and the Athletics overcame a six-run deficit to beat Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
In addition to the homer off Sam Bachman, Cortes also delivered a pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh, helping the Athletics end a six-game losing streak. Zack Gelof hit a two-run homer later in the eighth for the A's. Shea Langeliers and Lawrence Butler each had three hits and an RBI for the Athletics.
Denzer Guzman homered and drove in four RBIs for the Angels, who have lost four of their last six games. Mike Trout added three hits and two runs for Los Angeles (60-97), which has never lost 100 games in a season.
Blue Jays at Orioles, ppd.
The scheduled game between Toronto and host Baltimore was postponed due to ongoing inclement weather. The game will be made up as part of a split doubleheader on Wednesday, with games starting at 1:35 p.m. and 6:35 p.m. ET.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
MLB公式SNSの投稿が話題
【MLB】ドジャース 7ー0 パドレス（日本時間23日・ロサンゼルス） ドジャース・大谷翔平投手が、復帰を翌日に控えるなか、思わぬ形で登場した。MLB公式X（旧ツイッター）が22日（日本時間23日）に公開した1枚に“参戦”。チームを代表して現れた大谷に、ファンからは「めちゃかっこいい」と興奮の声があがった。 【実際の投稿】突如登場した大谷翔平…MLBが公開した「球界を代表する6つの顔」 MLB公式が突如公開したのは、すでにポストシーズン進出を決めた6球団を取り上げた特別画像。「究極の栄冠を目指して、あと6チームがその輪に加わる。10月（ポストシーズン）のような時期は他にない。もうすぐやってくる」とコメントが添えられた。進出が決まっているレイズ、ヤンキース、レッドソックス、ドジャース、ブルワーズ、ブレーブスから1人ずつが登場。ドジャースからは大谷が選ばれた。 大谷は15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）入りしているが、23日（同24日）にメジャー復帰が見込まれている。デーブ・ロバーツ監督は22日（同23日）のパドレス戦前、「明日になることを想定している。（異常を知らせる）何か聞かない限り、彼は明日スタメンで出場する」と、23日（同24日）の同戦でスタメン復帰する見通しだと言及。ポストシーズンを見据える中で、いよいよ戦列に戻ってくる。
復帰前日のタイミングで公開された大谷の“1枚”に日米ファンが反応。「球界を代表する6人の顔」「楽しみが増える」「この写真、かっこよすぎませんか？」「翔平様～頑張って」といった声が寄せられた。

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers leave door open to Edwin Diaz reclaiming closer’s role: ‘Certainly possible’
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

item.content:encoded:
In a perfect world, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, the team would like to have one set closer entering the playoffs.
And by the end of Tuesday’s 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, one unexpected name might have thrown their hat back into the ring.
A week ago, the Dodgers were not certain Edwin Díaz would even be on their playoff roster, after the $69 million offseason signing lost his closer job amid an injury-plagued season marred by an ERA of nearly 12.00.
In three outings since returning from the injured list, however, the three-time All-Star has suddenly looked like his old dominant self again.
So much so, Roberts said it remains “certainly possible” that he could factor into the Dodgers’ ninth-inning October plans.
Roberts made that claim after Díaz’s best performance yet, when he retired the top of the Padres’ batting order in order in a dominant fifth-inning sequence.
That marked the right-hander’s third scoreless appearance in a row –– a stretch that has included only one hit, one walk and six strikeouts –– and continued an unforeseen return to form triggered by a recent mechanical adjustment he made during a minor-league rehab stint.
“His last three have been fantastic with us,” Roberts said. “I wanted to see him against their better hitters, and he did a really nice job.”
Indeed, Díaz began his inning by ringing up Fernando Tatis Jr. on a front-door slider. He then fanned Dustin Harris at the end of a nine-pitch at-bat with a swing-and-miss slider. Had he used an ABS challenge, he could have punched out Manny Machado too. But he retired him all the same with a soft tapper back to the mound.
“Given all that he’s had to go through this year,” Roberts said, “to right the ship is a big credit to him.”
But will it be enough to put him back in consideration for closing duties?
Roberts made sure not to shut that door yet.
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” the manager said.
At the very least, it adds one more subplot to the final week of the Dodgers’ regular season.
The team, of course, has other closer options to consider. Tanner Scott has converted 23 of 27 save opportunities with a 2.77 ERA as Díaz’s replacement this year. Roki Sasaki has also returned to relief duties as he did at the end of last season, when he emerged as an emergency closing option during the Dodgers’ run to a second-straight World Series.
And as Roberts noted Tuesday, a closer-by-committee plan remains in play, as well.
But as the Dodgers set out for a three-peat this year, they always envisioned Díaz –– and his trademark trumpet bullpen entrance –– being a staple at the end of games.
Though he suffered a career-worst campaign, converting just seven of 11 save opportunities while missing three months with an elbow injury and another with neck inflammation, there might be time for him to reclaim his original role yet.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Tommy Edman y Will Smith conectaron jonrones, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles anotaron cinco carreras con dos outs para vencer el martes 7-0 a los Padres de San Diego en el primer juego de una serie entre rivales con los dos mejores récords de las Grandes Ligas este mes.
Los Dodgers (97-60) se colocaron a un juego del campeón de la División Central de la Liga Nacional, Milwaukee (98-59), por la mejor marca de las mayores y la ventaja de local durante toda la postemporada. Sin embargo, los Cerveceros poseen el desempate por enfrentamientos directos.
Los Ángeles necesita una victoria o que Atlanta pierda para asegurar un pase directo a la primera ronda y avanzar a la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Los Dodgers, campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional, mejoraron a 15-5 en septiembre con su quinta victoria consecutiva; los Padres cayeron a 14-5 y vieron cortada su racha de cinco triunfos.
El dominicano Fernando Tatis Jr. y Manny Machado, de San Diego, se combinaron para irse de 7-1 con cinco ponches.
Michael King (12-10) salió después de cuatro entradas en su 32da apertura de la temporada, la mayor cifra de su carrera. El derecho permitió cinco carreras y seis hits y ponchó a cinco, mientras se terminó su racha de cuatro victorias seguidas.

item.content:encoded:
What Shohei Ohtani's impending return means for Dodgers' lineup
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, Sept. 23, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 22. If that holds true, it would mean the Los Angeles Dodgers' franchise cornerstone would have five games to ramp up before the start of the postseason.
Ohtani, who has been on the 15-day IL retroactively since Sept. 8 due to lingering issues with his right bicep and left knee, took coach pitch batting practice and went through his normal workout routine on Tuesday ahead of a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres and according to the Dodgers skipper, he continues to check all the boxes necessary for a return.
"The thought is tomorrow," Roberts told reporters. "Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup tomorrow."
The Dodgers have gotten hot in Ohtani's absence, posting an 8-3 record since Sept. 11 – the day he was placed on the IL – and outscoring their opponents 59-28 in that timeframe. They enter Wednesday on a five-game winning streak, have already won the NL West and their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is down to 1. Ohtani will have the opportunity to find his footing in low-stakes games to finish out the regular season. That's huge considering he did not face live pitching in his hitting progression. But what does his impending return mean for the rest of the Dodgers lineup?
Catcher Eliezer Alfonzo was optioned on Tuesday as center fielder Andy Pages made his return. Alex Freeland could be a candidate to get optioned with rookie Josue De Paula, who is in the middle of an impressive "trial run" in his first shot at the big leagues and making a serious push at making the playoff roster. If he does play in October, it would likely be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Dalton Rushing, who has been on the IL since Sept. 6 with right elbow discomfort, is also expected to be activated soon and will battle with De Paula for that spot over the final five games, though Roberts acknowledged that Rushing is at a disadvantage with a small window to show what he can do.
"It’s not a knock on him," Roberts told reporters. "He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision."
Whatever the decision ends up being, a red-hot Dodgers offense with Ohtani at the top of it – though Roberts has said he'd consider keeping Mookie Betts batting leadoff against lefties – suddenly makes them one of the toughest matchups this October just when they were looking like they were in their most vulnerable state just weeks ago.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers extend home winning streak to 11 with shutout of Padres
(Photo credit: William Liang)
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs and the Los Angeles Dodgers inched closer to the best record in the National League with a 7-0 victory over the visiting San Diego Padres in the opener of a three-game series Tuesday.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles fell one game behind the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the NL Division Series to one.
Rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula had two hits with a run scored for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani expected to return from a biceps injury as a hitter Wednesday.
Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two. Right-hander Michael King (12-10) gave up five runs on six hits over four innings, his most runs allowed in a start since May 30.
It was just the second loss in 15 games for San Diego, which is close to locking up a third consecutive playoff berth for the first time in franchise history.
The Dodgers took advantage of King's loss of command to start a four-run outburst in the second inning, all with two outs. The Dodgers loaded the bases on two singles and a hit batter, while Edman and Mookie Betts both walked to force in runs.
Freeman followed Betts with a two-run single for a 4-0 lead.
Freeman added a run-scoring single in the fourth inning, while Edman hit a home run in the sixth and Smith hit his in the seventh. Edman homered for the second straight game, while Smith went deep in his third consecutive start.
'The Dodgers welcomed back Andy Pages from a broken left hand, and he was hit by a pitch and drew a walk in four plate appearances.
--Field Level Media

The Dodgers are pouring it on.
How about this work from the Dodger bullpen tonight?
Seven pitchers have combined for eight scoreless innings, and Jack Dreyer tries to finish it off.
Two down in the top of the ninth.
Ground ball to short, Mookie Betts.
Eight pitchers, nine innings, no runs.
The Dodgers shut out the Padres in a bullpen game to open up this series.
And that will ensure that the Padres begin tomorrow as they began today, with a magic number of two.

item.title: [ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos] Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
item.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
item.dc:creator: ABC News; BETH HARRIS AP sports writer
item.description: Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best recor
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month
LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month.
The Dodgers (97-60) moved within one game of NL Central champion Milwaukee (98-59) for the top mark in the big leagues and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. However, the Brewers own the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Los Angeles needs one win or an Atlanta loss to clinch a first-round bye into a National League Division Series.
The NL West champion Dodgers improved to 15-5 in September with their fifth straight victory; the Padres fell to 14-5 and had their five-game winning streak snapped.
San Diego is tied with Chicago and Philadelphia at 87-70 for the three NL wild cards — four games ahead of Arizona with five to play.
Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado were a combined 1 for 7 with five strikeouts for the Padres.
The Dodgers chased Michael King (12-10) after four innings in his career-high 32nd start of the season. The right-hander gave up five runs on six hits and struck out five as his four-game winning streak ended.
Los Angeles broke out with four runs in the second. King got the first two outs on six pitches before loading the bases. Teoscar Hernández and rookie Josue De Paula hit consecutive singles before King plunked Andy Pages, who just came off the injured list.
King then issued back-to-back walks to Edman and Mookie Betts, forcing in two runs. Freddie Freeman's two-run single made it 4-0.
Betts had a ground-rule double and scored on Freeman's two-out single for a 5-0 lead in the fourth.
Edman's solo shot came with two outs in the sixth and Smith added a 396-foot drive with one out in the seventh for a 7-0 lead.
Brock Stewart started a bullpen game and Justin Wrobleski (12-5) got the win for the Dodgers, who used eight pitchers to earn the fifth shutout in franchise history when deploying at least that many.
Among them was reliever Edwin Díaz, who struck out two in one inning. Roki Sasaki's four-seam fastball touched 100 mph while he pitched one inning. The Japanese right-hander came off the injured list earlier Tuesday after missing nearly a month with a blister on his right middle finger.
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA) starts Wednesday against Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51).
___
This story has been corrected to show the Dodgers scored six runs with two outs, not five.
___

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Roki Sasaki llamó la atención cuando pasó al bullpen durante la marcha del año pasado hacia el bicampeonato. Volverá a desempeñar ese papel en los últimos días de esta temporada regular y posiblemente vuelva a estar entre las opciones para cerrar juegos.
Sasaki fue activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días antes de la victoria por 7-0 sobre los Padres la noche del martes, como parte de una serie de movimientos que también incluyeron el regreso del cubano Andy Pagés de la lista de lesionados y el envío de Emmet Sheehan y el venezolano Eliezer Alfonzo a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sasaki lanzó por última vez el 26 de agosto, cuando una ampolla en el dedo medio de la mano derecha puso fin prematuramente a su apertura contra los Bravos.
En su segunda temporada en Grandes Ligas, Sasaki se acercaba cada vez más a la versión de sí mismo que fue un fenómeno en la Liga Japonesa de Béisbol Profesional (NPB, por sus siglas en inglés). Tuvo marca de 5-5 con efectividad de 4.60 en 23 aperturas, pero esos números no cuentan toda la historia. Con un repertorio más amplio, que incluye un nuevo splitter, y una mayor velocidad en su recta, Sasaki tuvo su mejor tramo sostenido como abridor en Grandes Ligas, registrando efectividad de 2.63 en siete aperturas antes de lidiar con la ampolla.
“Emocionado de tener a Roki de vuelta”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Está entusiasmado con este rol. Creo que puede tener un gran impacto, como lo tuvo el año pasado”.
En su regreso al bullpen el martes, Sasaki ponchó a dos en un cuarto inning en blanco, pese a permitir un par de sencillos con dos outs. Generó cuatro swings fallidos, incluidos dos en igual número de swings contra su splitter, y promedió 98.7 mph con las ocho rectas que lanzó, ligeramente por encima de su promedio de 97.8 mph esta temporada.
Los Dodgers mejoraron su récord a 97-60 después de que su juego de bullpen terminara en blanqueada. Están cinco juegos por delante de los Bravos en la lucha por el segundo mejor récord de la Liga Nacional y a uno de los Cerveceros, líderes del circuito y dueños del criterio de desempate entre ambos.
El año pasado, el traslado de Sasaki al relevo fue una decisión sin precedentes. Después de un comienzo por debajo de las expectativas en su temporada de novato y de perderse más de cuatro meses por una lesión en el hombro, la única oportunidad de Sasaki de contribuir con los Dodgers en la postemporada era pasar al bullpen.
Sasaki no sólo contribuyó, sino que se convirtió en el cerrador de los Dodgers en la postemporada, permitiendo apenas una carrera limpia en 10.2 innings, para efectividad de 0.84. La confianza que adquirió al conseguir resultados en Grandes Ligas, bajo la máxima presión, impulsó el regreso del derecho de 24 años a la rotación y su posterior despegue a mitad de esta temporada.
Actualmente, los Dodgers no cuentan con un cerrador fijo, ya que el boricua Edwin Díaz está lanzando en situaciones de baja presión en medio de sus dificultades a lo largo de la temporada, mientras busca ganarse un puesto en el bullpen para la postemporada. Díaz ponchó a dos en un quinto inning perfecto la noche del martes, su tercera presentación sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
Ha pasado mucho tiempo desde que Sasaki lanzó como relevista, pero si logra mostrarle lo suficiente a Roberts durante la última semana antes de la postemporada, podría convertirse en una opción para situaciones de salvamento.
“Creo que sin duda es una opción”, dijo Roberts. “Probablemente mucho dependerá de cómo lance esta noche. Seguramente tendrá una o dos presentaciones cortas más antes de que termine la temporada”.
Con Díaz perdiendo tiempo de juego por lesiones en el codo y el cuello, además de no lanzar bien cuando estuvo saludable, el zurdo Tanner Scott ha recibido la mayoría de las oportunidades de salvamento. Scott lidera a los Dodgers con 23 rescates, pero también ha desperdiciado cuatro oportunidades, incluidas dos desde comienzos de septiembre.
Scott todavía podría ser la mejor opción para cerrar los juegos, pero Sasaki podría complementarlo desde el lado derecho, algo importante debido a que el derecho venezolano Edgardo Henríquez estará fuera por el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la parte baja de la espalda. Se espera que regrese durante la postemporada.
Aunque a Roberts le gustaría contar con un cerrador en la postemporada, reconoció que es más probable que maneje el bullpen según los enfrentamientos. En esta época del año, algunas de las situaciones de mayor presión se presentan antes del noveno inning, por lo que tener varias opciones le permitiría utilizar a sus mejores relevistas en los momentos más convenientes.
“Creo que si hay una oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner lance un inning de alta presión en el séptimo u octavo, es difícil dejarla pasar si es la mejor opción en ese momento”, dijo Roberts. “Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se va a presentar el noveno inning”.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers shutout of Padres reveals potential (and unexpected) playoff strength
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs. This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint. In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. item.content:encoded:
Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs.
This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint.
In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are.
And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings.
However, replicating the starting pitching excellence of last October won’t be easy. A season ago, the Dodgers’ four-man rotation of Ohtani, Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow accounted for 113 of the team’s 165 postseason innings (including relief appearances from Glasnow and Yamamoto). Together, they posted a 2.55 ERA.
It was historic production.
Which also means, it’s fair to assume some regression will be possible –– both in workload and effectiveness.
Thus, having more reliable bullpen options this time around could be equally important for the Dodgers. And while that might have felt like a daunting reality earlier this year, when the unit was banged up and struggling through the middle portion of the campaign, Tuesday night was a reminder that the relief corps could be a strength in this fall’s title pursuit.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.”
In a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, the Dodgers were not supposed to have the pitching matchup –– countering Padres ace Michael King with a makeshift bullpen game in a rivalry series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Instead, eight different Dodgers relievers held the previous red-hot Padres to a five-hit shutout. Along the way, several arms who once seemed like question marks continued to round into increasingly promising form.
“It was fantastic,” Roberts said. “This is as good as our bullpen has been, has thrown.”
It started with opener Brock Stewart, a key right-handed weapon in the Dodgers’ bullpen who began the game with a scoreless first inning, continuing his late-season resurgence after another injury-plagued year.
From there, the baton was passed on down.
Justin Wrobleski, who is in the midst of a late-season conversion to the bullpen for the second-straight year, escaped a jam in the second. Blake Treinen, who might be on the postseason roster bubble given the Dodgers’ relief depth, offered one of his best outings of late by issuing only a two-out walk in a scoreless third.
Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters
California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedIn
California Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X
California Post Opinion
California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!
California Post App: Download here!
Home delivery: Sign up here!
Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!
The highlight of the night came in the fourth and fifth, when Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz hung a couple more zeroes in what were important appearances from each.
For Sasaki, the outing marked his first since returning from the injured list and making his own late-season move back to the bullpen, where he could reprise his role as closer from last year’s playoffs. He worked around a pair of singles with two strikeouts and a fastball that, even after being sidelined for the last month by a blister, sat at 99-100 mph.
For Díaz, Tuesday was not only a third-consecutive scoreless outing since his own return from the IL, but his most impressive yet as he makes a bid for the playoff roster. He retired the top of the Padres lineup in order with a pair of strikeouts, and has now retired 9 of 11 batters he has faced since rejoining the active roster.
Asked postgame if Díaz –– the $69 million offseason signing who lost the closer’s job amid a previously dismal debut Dodgers season –– could still pitch his way back into ninth-inning duties, Roberts said it’s “certainly possible.”
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” Roberts added.
By that point, the Dodgers had already pulled away from the Padres. They mounted a four-run rally with two outs in the second against King, who issued back-to-back bases-loaded walks to Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts before Freddie Freeman slashed a two-run single through the infield. The offense tacked on more runs in the fourth (on another Freeman RBI single), the sixth (on a solo home run from Tommy Edman), and the seventh (a Will Smith solo blast).
In what was the lineup’s toughest test in a while, they passed with flying colors.
Still, the night’s most encouraging developments came from the ‘pen, which capped off the game with two scoreless innings from Kyle Hurt, then stress-free appearances in the eighth and ninth from Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer.
The unit’s most trusted arms at the moment, Tanner Scott (who figures to be vying with Sasaki for the postseason closer role) and Evan Phillips, weren’t even required. Nor was Edgardo Henriquez, who remains sidelined by a back injury but still could return in time for the playoffs.
“We know we have a good group, and anytime we get to carry the load and everybody has success and throws up zeros, it’s special,” Stewart said. “That’s really hard to do, for all eight guys or whatever it was today. So yeah, it’s cool.”
With a smirk, he added: “Write stories about it.”
Come October, of course, the Dodgers will be hoping their relievers are the main story.
But if the rotation falters, the club seems significantly better-suited to handle it than it did a year ago.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know,” Roberts said. “But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”

item.content:encoded:
【パドレス0-7ドジャース】ロサンゼルス／ドジャースタジアム、9月22日（日本時間23日）
すでに地区優勝とポストシーズン進出を決めているドジャースは本拠地でのパドレス3連戦がスタート。その初戦はブルペンゲームの投手陣を打線がしっかり援護し、7-0で快勝して5連勝となった。メジャー最高勝率のブルワーズが敗れたため、ドジャースはブルワーズまで1ゲーム差に接近。負傷者リストから復帰した佐々木朗希は4番手として四回に登板し、2安打を浴びながらも1イニングを無失点に抑えた（防御率4.56）。 ドジャースは先発のブロック・スチュワートと2番手のジャスティン・ロブレスキーが各1イニングを無失点に抑えると、二回2死からヒット2本と死球で満塁のチャンスを作り、トミー・エドマンとムーキー・ベッツが2者連続で押し出し四球を選んで2点を先制。さらにフレディ・フリーマンの2点タイムリーが飛び出し、4-0とリードした。 三回を3番手のブレイク・トライネンが無失点に抑え、四回は佐々木が登板。ジャクソン・メリルをセンターフライ、オースティン・ヘイズを空振り三振に仕留め、簡単に2死を取ったあと、連打で一、二塁のピンチとなったが、ジェイク・クロネンワースを見逃し三振に仕留め、無失点で切り抜けた。 その直後、ドジャースは2死からベッツが二塁打を放ってチャンスメイクし、フリーマンのタイムリーで1点を追加。五回は5番手のエドウィン・ディアスが三者凡退に抑える好リリーフを見せ、六回は6番手のカイル・ハートが無失点に抑えた。 すると、六回2死からトミー・エドマンの8号ソロで1点を追加。ハートは回跨ぎで七回も無失点に抑え、直後にウィル・スミスにも10号ソロが飛び出して7-0とリードを広げた。 八回は7番手のアレックス・ベシアがマウンドに上がり、2死から四球を与えたものの、メリルを空振り三振に仕留めて無失点。九回は8番手のジャック・ドライヤーが三者凡退に抑える好リリーフを見せ、8人の投手による完封リレーを締めくくった。 勝利したドジャースは最高勝率ブルワーズまで1ゲーム差に接近。ただし、ブルワーズとの直接対決で負け越しているため、第1シードでポストシーズンに進むためにはブルワーズを勝率で上回る必要がある。

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers rout Padres in bulk in opener
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular season. The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a bye into the NLDS is down to just one.
King hadn’t allowed more than three runs in any of his previous nine starts, with a 2.26 ERA during that span, and he retired his first five batters faced on Tuesday. Then with two outs in the second inning, the next six batters reached, breaking open the scoring.
Teoscar Hernández singles for the Dodgers’ first hit, then Josue De Paula singled on an 0-2 pitch before Andy Pages was hit by a pitch in his very first plate appearance back since getting hit by a pitch one month prior, to load the bases. Tommy Edman walked on four pitches for the game’s first run, Mookie Betts only needed five pitches to walk home another run, then Freddie Freeman grounded a single through the infield, and under the legs of a leaping Edman, to score two more.
Betts hit a ground-rule double in the fourth, followed by another RBI single by Freeman for a fifth run against King.
Solo home runs by Edman in the sixth and Will Smith in the seventh off the Padres bullpen padded the scoring.
With Emmet Sheehan optioned on Tuesday and Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, the Dodgers have only three active pitchers they plan to use as starting pitchers in the postseason at the moment. That means they have 11 relievers, and on a day following an off day and the day before a start by the MLB leader in innings per start, the Dodgers used .. pitchers to cover the nine innings.
Starters Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki — the latter just activated on Tuesday — each pitched only one inning, both scoreless. Sasaki was hitting 100 mph in his first game action in four weeks.
Kyle Hurt was the only Dodgers pitcher to toss more than one inning, taking care of the sixth and seventh.
Jack Dreyer was the first pitcher of Sunday’s game, and the last pitcher on Tuesday.
It’s only the third time in franchise history the Dodgers used eight pitchers in a shutout of no more than nine innings, done also on September 29, 2019 in San Francisco and May 15 this year in Anaheim. For some perspective, when the Dodgers beat the Expos 1-0 Montreal in 22 innings on August 23, 1989 — Rick Dempsey homered, Tommy Lasorda got Expos mascot Youppi ejected — the Dodgers only used five pitchers that day.
Tuesday particulars
Home runs: Tommy Edman (8), Will Smith (10)
WP — Justin Wrobleski (12-5): 1 IP, 1 hit
LP — Michael King (12-10): 4 IP, 6 hits, 5 runs, 2 walks, 5 strikeouts

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dalton Rushing Faces Dodgers Postseason Roster Battle
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Dalton Rushing may have only three regular-season games to convince the Los Angeles Dodgers that he should be their left-handed bat off the bench in October. Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Tuesday that Rushing’s missed time creates a difficult path as the Dodgers compare him with top prospect Josue De Paula for a potential postseason bench role. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Dalton Rushing may have only three regular-season games to convince the Los Angeles Dodgers that he should be their left-handed bat off the bench in October.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Tuesday that Rushing’s missed time creates a difficult path as the Dodgers compare him with top prospect Josue De Paula for a potential postseason bench role. De Paula’s recent run of consistent at-bats gives him an important advantage entering the final week.
“It’s going to be tougher for Dalton, given the time that he’s missed,” Roberts said. “To think that you have three games to get back into playoff form—which is tough to do.”
Rushing has resumed taking at-bats as he works back from the right elbow discomfort that sent him to the injured list earlier this month. Roberts said the Dodgers hope to activate him at some point during the final series of the regular season, giving the club a brief opportunity to evaluate how he looks as a pinch-hitting option.
What the Dodgers will evaluate
The Dodgers are looking beyond raw results as they decide which left-handed hitter gives them the better postseason option. Roberts said the evaluation will focus on the quality and structure of each plate appearance.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, obviously the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts said. “There’s potential slug with both those guys.”
Producing off the bench presents a different challenge from playing every day. A postseason reserve might receive one plate appearance against a premium reliever and be expected to control the strike zone without the benefit of several earlier at-bats.
That makes recent game action especially important. De Paula has remained active since making the jump from Double-A to the Dodgers, while Rushing must attempt to recover his timing immediately after another interruption to his season.
“It’s not, again, a knock on him,” Roberts said of Rushing. “He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, given also where you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue.”
No postseason roster decision yet
Roberts did not declare De Paula the winner of the roster competition. He called the comparison “a good debate” and said the Dodgers still need to discuss which hitter gives them the best chance in a limited bench role.
Rushing’s immediate path is expected to come as a hitter rather than a catcher. If he is activated for the final three games, every plate appearance could carry added weight as the Dodgers finalize their postseason roster.
De Paula has already impressed the organization during his first major-league opportunity. Rushing, however, offers his own combination of strike-zone control and power. The final decision could come down to whether three games provide enough evidence that his timing has returned.

item.title: [tsn.ca] Ohtani 'considerably' healthier, expected back in Dodgers' lineup Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Wednesday, the first day he is eligible to be activated off the injured list, and Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he looks "considerably" healthier than he did a couple of weeks ago. "If he was a five, he's probably an eight or a nine right now," Roberts said, referencing a 1-to-10 scale. The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the lead
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani is expected to return to the lineup Wednesday, the first day he is eligible to be activated off the injured list, and Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts says he looks "considerably" healthier than he did a couple of weeks ago.
"If he was a five, he's probably an eight or a nine right now," Roberts said, referencing a 1-to-10 scale.
The Dodgers activated right-hander Roki Sasaki and center fielder Andy Pages off the IL on Tuesday, a major development in the leadup to October.
Sasaki, who has been recovering from a blister suffered in an Aug. 26 start, was available out of the bullpen for Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres and could be an option to again close out games in the postseason. Pages, who fractured his left hand on Aug. 22, will reprise his role as an everyday player at a premium position.
Ohtani landed on the IL because of lingering pain in his right biceps and left knee on Sept. 8 but began a hitting progression seven days ago and advanced to taking as many as 40 swings off Trajekt, the popular pitching simulator, on Saturday. Ohtani also ran the bases that day. On Tuesday, he went through his typical pregame workout.
Ohtani, 32, will only hit the rest of this season and was struggling in that realm before landing on the IL, compiling only seven hits and 22 strikeouts over his past 54 at-bats. Roberts previously indicated the plan was for Ohtani to play in all of the Dodgers' remaining five regular-season games to get reacclimated to major league pitching.
Where he hits, though, is up for debate. In all likelihood, Ohtani will continue to lead off against opposing right-handed pitchers. But Mookie Betts' recent hot streak -- heading into this week, he was hitting.373/.468/.746 in September -- has Roberts weighing the possibility of batting him leadoff against lefties.
What Ohtani's return means for outfield prospect Josue De Paula is also an open question.
De Paula, 21, has eight hits and 10 walks in 38 plate appearances since temporarily replacing Ohtani at designated hitter. The Dodgers are strongly considering him as an option to be a left-handed bat off the bench during the postseason, though they might send him down as the corresponding move for activating Ohtani to give him at-bats in this week's Triple-A championship series.
The other candidate would be backup catcher Dalton Rushing, who has an elbow injury that is preventing him from throwing. Rushing is expected to be activated at some point in the next three days, but Roberts acknowledged it would be difficult for him to be thrust into a pinch-hitting role in October after playing in only four games since the start of September.
"There's potential slug with both those guys," Roberts said. "It's going to be a good debate."

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Veteran infielder Miguel Rojas was voted by his Dodgers teammates and coaching staff as the 2026 winner of the Roy Campanella Award, given annually to the Dodgers player who best embodies the leadership and spirit of the Hall of Fame catcher. Rojas also won the award in 2024 and 2025, making him the first player to win the Campanella Award in three straight seasons.
In the 21-year history of the award, Justin Turner is the only other player to win the Campanella Award three times, taking the honor in 2017, 2019, and 2020. Clayton Kershaw (2013-14) and Chase Utley (2016, 2018) are the only other Dodgers to win the award twice.
The 37-year-old Rojas was the first Dodgers player to speak ahead of the clubhouse celebration last Thursday in Cincinnati when the Dodgers clinched the National League West.
The longtime shortstop Rojas has started games at second base, shortstop, and third base this season, and even played three innings at first base. He's hitting .271/.311/.399 with a 93 wRC+ in his 101 games and 243 plate appearances, including a robust .297/.340/.476 with a 122 wRC+ against left-handed pitchers.
The Dodgers traded for Rojas prior to the 2023 season, and he has mentored young players and filled in all over the infield for the last four seasons. Rojas cemented his place in Dodgers lore with his game-tying home run in the ninth inning of Game 7 of the 2025 World Series at Toronto.
Rojas signed a one-year, $5.5 million contract in December to return for his 13th and final season, and plans to join the Dodgers front office afterward, with a focus on player development. Rojas has long stated his desire to get into coaching once his playing days are over.
"Nobody when I came to this organization asked me, 'Hey we want you to be a leader' or 'We want you to be a mentor.' It's just who I want to be and who I want to be for the future," Rojas told True Blue LA in 2024. "After my career is over, I'm trying to stay on the field, to stay coaching, and I want to be a part of an organization that wants to win."
Rojas will receive his 2026 Roy Campanella Award before Thursday night's series finale against the Padres, with Campanella's daughter, Joni Campanella Roan, and his granddaughter, Akua Campanella presenting Rojas with the award on the field at Dodger Stadium.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — It’s the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round.
Before Tuesday’s game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday’s start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Francisco against the Giants, with Tarik Skubal — currently on the bereavement list — starting Friday night at Oracle Park.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto starts Wednesday and Tyler Glasnow Thursday against the Padres.
Also on Tuesday, reliever Will Klein pitched a simulated inning against Dalton Rushing in a battle of players on the injured list. Klein is on the 60-day injured list with elbow discomfort and not eligible to be activated until September 30 at the earliest, but it looks like he’ll be in the stay-hot camp should the Dodgers have room to add him at some point later in the postseason, similar to in 2025 when Klein wasn’t active until the World Series and he pitched five scoreless innings, including four innings in the marathon Game 3.
“With Will it’s more get healthy, show that you’re healthy, throw to some hitters,” Roberts said. “He’ll throw during the week off, then we’ll kind of see if there’s an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year.”
Rushing is trying to work his way back from elbow discomfort suffered when practicing throwing. His role would be a left-handed bat off the bench, a role currently occupied by Josue De Paula, who has been the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out. But Ohtani is expected to be activated Wednesday barring an unforeseen setback.
That essentially sets up a battle between Rushing and De Paula for a postseason roster spot, though Roberts said the plan is to activate Rushing at some point this week to literally get back into the swing of things.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat obviously, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit. There’s potential slug with both guys. I think it’s a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult so we’re trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“And to be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Activating both Ohtani and Rushing this week, when the Dodgers have 14 active position players, would require two corresponding moves to make room on the active roster. If De Paula doesn’t get sent down — “I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday — that might mean rough news for Alexes Call and Freeland, either this week or next.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Se espera que Shohei Ohtani vuelva a la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles el miércoles tras una etapa en la lista de lesionados.
La superestrella ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde el 9 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y a un dolor persistente en la rodilla izquierda.
El mánager Dave Roberts comentó que Ohtani se siente “considerablemente” mejor.
“Yo diría que si estaba en un cinco, ahora probablemente está en un ocho o un nueve”, manifestó Roberts el martes antes de que los Dodgers enfrentaran a San Diego.
Los Dodgers aseguraron su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años sin Ohtani, quien estaba en Los Ángeles recibiendo tratamiento cuando el equipo venció a Cincinnati como visitante la semana pasada. Ahora, el cuatro veces MVP tendrá cinco juegos restantes para tomar algunos turnos al bate antes de que comience la postemporada.
Es probable que Ohtani retome su papel como primer bate de los Dodgers, especialmente contra lanzadores derechos. Mookie Betts ha estado encabezando la alineación y batea para .373 este mes.
“Probablemente así es como va a quedar, pero todavía no lo he decidido del todo”, señaló Roberts, y añadió que consideraría el valor de Betts como primer bate contra lanzadores zurdos. “Tengo que pensar en toda la estructura de la alineación”.
___

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been without superstar slugger Shohei Ohtani for the last week+ as he's been dealing with a biceps issue that led to his IL placement.
Manager Dave Roberts indicated on Tuesday, before the Dodgers' series opener with the San Diego Padres, that Ohtani will be activated from the IL on Wednesday.
However, in Ohtani's absence, the Dodgers have implemented infielder Mookie Betts in the leadoff spot, and Mookie has been on fire at the plate, which leaves Roberts at a crossroads.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Good Blake Snell News Before Padres Game
Dave Roberts Reveals Tough Decision Ahead with Leadoff Batter
Dave Roberts indicated to the media on Tuesday evening that he isn't entirely sure who will lead off between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani when Ohtani returns from the IL.
"Dave Roberts said he is still debating who will lead off when Ohtani returns, but said it will most likely be dependent upon pitching matchups So, Ohtani vs RHP and Mookie Betts vs LHP"
It might be wise for the Dodgers to get Shohei Ohtani in a different role, as he's been slumping over the past month+.
As for Mookie Betts, he's starting to hit an offensive stride after struggling for most of the season.
It will be very interesting to see how Roberts handles Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani's lineup spots in the last week of the regular season.
Dodgers reporter Bill Plunkett wrote (about the situation):
"Dave Roberts said "as of now" Shohei Ohtani will return to the leadoff spot when he comes off IL Wednesday but it's something he is giving further thought to. Could be a case where Ohtani hits first v RH Betts v LH"

item.content:encoded:
The Athletics’ spoiler magic ran out last week, as the team dropped all six games of its final road trip against the first-place Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays. Tonight, the A’s open the last week of the season with the first of two matchups against the Los Angeles Angels, with both teams trying to avoid finishing at the bottom of the American League West standings.
Additionally, with a looming offseason lockout leaving the fate of the 2027 season up in the air, this week may mark the end of the Athletics’ time in Sacramento, which served as a placeholder while their new stadium in Las Vegas gets built. All the more reason for the A’s to try to close out 2026 with a winning homestand.
Roster Move
Before the game, the A’s made a roster move.
Rookie infielder Joshua Kuroda-Grauer has recovered from a ruptured testicle to rejoin the Athletics for the remainder of the season. He spent the past few days on a rehab assignment with the franchise’s Triple-A affiliate, the Las Vegas Aviators, who begin their quest for the Pacific Coast League championship today.
To make room for him, fellow infielder Max Muncy lands on the injured list with left knee chondromalacia, also known as runner’s knee. Additionally, J.T. Ginn, who was shut down for the season a couple of weeks ago, moves to the 60-day injured list.
Game Preview
Back to the game, left-hander Brady Basso will get the A’s final homestand underway. The 28-year-old enters his 25th appearance and seventh opener assignment of the season with a 1-3 record, a 4.50 ERA, a 1.48 WHIP and 28 strikeouts in 40 innings.
Tonight will be Basso’s third consecutive outing as his team’s opener. Two starts ago, he pitched four scoreless innings against the Toronto Blue Jays. However, the southpaw struggled in his most recent outing against the Tampa Bay Rays, allowing four runs on seven hits over 2 2/3 innings.
The A’s will hope Basso pitches as well as he did in his last home game. Yesterday’s off day means the team’s league-worst bullpen is well-rested should Basso’s second career appearance and first start against the Angels only last a couple innings.
Here’s the A’s lineup for the series opener:
At the very least, this lineup should ensure the A’s will be defensively sound, with no players being asked to play out of position. Kuroda-Grauer, who will hopefully remember his cup this time, immediately finds himself in the starting nine at second base. His MLB career was off to a hot start before he suffered the unfortunate injury. Will JKG pick up where he left off, or will he be rusty after spending weeks on the sidelines?
Further down the lineup, center fielder Denzel Clarke receives a rare start to showcase his athleticism on the baseball field. Everyone knows how good a fielder Clarke is, but the jury is still out on whether he will hit enough to warrant a full-time spot on a major league roster. If the A’s want to win, they will need offensive production from Clarke, shortstop Alika Williams and five-hole hitter Tommy White.
The A’s offense will face Angels left-hander Yusei Kikuchi, who is finishing up an injury-plagued campaign. The 35-year-old enters his 13th start of the season with a 1-6 record, a 5.02 ERA, a 1.55 WHIP and 58 strikeouts over 57 1/3 innings.
Tuesday night will be Kikuchi’s first start against the Athletics this season. He has gone 3-5 with a 4.20 ERA and 63 strikeouts in 14 appearances vs. the A’s in his career. Last year, the veteran went 1-2 in three games against the Green and Gold.
And Los Angeles’ starting nine:
The Angels’ lineup quality drops dramatically after Zach Neto and Mike Trout at the top of the order. First baseman Vaughn Grissom has had a solid season, while catcher Moisés Ballesteros was one of the well-known prospects the team acquired during its trade-deadline selloff.
Time to start this final homestand strong and avoid another last-place finish in the division. Let’s go, A’s!

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Roki Sasaki Could Close for Dodgers in Postseason
item.dc:creator: Los Royers
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Roki Sasaki could pitch his way into the Los Angeles Dodgers’ closer conversation before the postseason begins.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday that using Sasaki as a closer in October is an option, although the Dodgers have not assigned him the ninth inning—or any fixed relief role—as he returns from the injured list.
“It’s certainly an option,” Roberts said. “A lot of it probably is contingent on how he throws here tonight.”
Sasaki was activated with Andy Pages before the Dodgers opened their series against the San Diego Padres. Rather than returning to the rotation, the right-hander will spend the final week auditioning for a postseason bullpen role.
Dodgers will evaluate Sasaki in multiple roles
Roberts said Sasaki could work two innings in his first appearance, entering at the start of a clean inning. That opportunity could arrive early, in the middle innings or late in the game depending on how the matchup develops.
“I could envision him pitching multiples,” Roberts said. “I can see him coming into a clean inning and pitching two innings. I’m not sure if that’s the third inning or the sixth inning or the eighth inning, but he’s ready.”
The Dodgers then expect to give Sasaki one or two shorter appearances before the regular season ends. Those outings will help determine whether he can handle a traditional closing assignment, provide multiple innings or fill another high-leverage role in October.
Roberts stopped short of labeling Sasaki the closer and noted that his late-inning success last season developed from the Dodgers’ needs at the time.
“I don’t want to say he’s going to finish games or be a closer,” Roberts said. “Last year was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance, with health of guys, and he filled that role admirably.”
Dodgers do not have a designated closer
Sasaki’s opportunity comes as the Dodgers prepare to enter October without one reliever locked into the ninth inning. Roberts said he would prefer a set closer in a perfect scenario, but he does not currently see one pitcher holding that job.
“Right now, I don’t see a one-person closer,” Roberts said.
That approach would allow Roberts to deploy Tanner Scott against the most dangerous portion of an opponent’s lineup before the ninth rather than saving him for a lead that might never materialize. Roberts also said he would be comfortable asking Evan Phillips or Brock Stewart to close a game.
Phillips has looked more like himself over his last three appearances following an inconsistent beginning to his return from Tommy John surgery, according to Roberts. Stewart has also been one of the Dodgers’ most effective relievers when healthy.
The Dodgers therefore have several ninth-inning possibilities. Sasaki’s final regular-season appearances will determine whether he becomes one of their most prominent options.

item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers’ Dalton Rushing will have chance to make case for postseason roster spot
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers plan to give catcher Dalton Rushing a chance to make his case for a spot on the postseason roster, after playing just four games in the last seven weeks because of a right elbow injury.
He’s set to be activated from the injured list before the end of the season, manager Dave Roberts said, and he’ll serve as a left-handed bat off the bench.
“Just showing them that I can swing it, and it’s an option,” Rushing told The Times after taking live batting practice Tuesday for the first time since landing on the IL earlier this month. “I know that you kind of tie [the team’s] hands up when you can’t play defense. So, I’m not expecting anything… just continue to take at-bats and see where we go from there.”
The slight tear in Rushing’s ulnar collateral ligament made headlines after he landed on the IL on Aug. 3. But Rushing’s MRI scans suggest the UCL — which is associated with Tommy John surgery — is not the issue.
The pain in his elbow seems to stem from a flexor strain. The small tear in his UCL has remained the same size since 2022, he said.
Rushing received platelet-rich plasma injection after aggravating the flexor injury a second time while working through a throwing program at the beginning of the month.
“I’m pretty confident I can still avoid surgery after the shot,” he said, noting that he’s been getting regular scans to monitor his healing. “Obviously, when I re-injured it the second time, I was almost 70-30, thinking that I was for sure going to need surgery. But after I got the shot and it ran its course, I feel as close to healthy in my arm as I have in a pretty long time.”
It was Josue De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the IL. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot.
This time, Rushing has abandoned the throwing program. But he said he doesn’t regret trying to return to the field the first time around.
“In my eyes, me trying to throw is me showing them that obviously I want to help the team win,” he said. “I want to give us the best available option that we have at that moment, and that was my whole plan all along. So I hope they see there wasn’t any selfishness in that.”
The Dodgers will need a left-handed bat off the bench in October, but Rushing now has competition.
Rookie Josue De Paula replaced Shohei Ohtani on the roster when the superstar landed on the 15-day IL two weeks ago. His first major-league hit was a three-run home run, and he entered Tuesday with a .974 OPS in 10 games.
Even if the Dodgers option De Paula on Wednesday when they reinstate Ohtani, 10 days before the NL Division Series, he will be eligible to be added to the NLDS roster via petition to the Commissioner’s Office.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“It’s going to be a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult, and so you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed, and … you have three games to get back in the playoff form, which is tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us. But it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Rushing played a large role in the Dodgers’ regular season. In his second year in the majors, he was thrust into the primary role behind the plate for two months because of Will Smith’s lingering neck injury. Now, he might not see the field in the postseason.
“It sucks,” he said of the injury derailing him down the stretch. “I mean, that’s really the only thing I can say about it, it’s not what I wanted — by no means.”
Looking beyond the playoffs, Rushing plans to evaluate his routine, hoping to set himself up to be available for more of 2027.
“I don’t even want to talk about it right now because we still have obviously a bigger task at hand,” Rushing said. “But my main plan moving into playing every day in the future is, make sure that my body can hold whatever stress or whatever is needed for this team — first base, behind the plate, whatever they need. I want to make sure my body can handle it and do it for 162.”

item.title: [MLB.com] Pages returns from IL, solidifying Dodgers' defense just in time for October
item.dc:creator: Courtney Hollmon
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers got their center fielder back on Tuesday, but they aren't expecting Andy Pages to immediately pick up where he left off at the plate. And right now, they don't necessarily need him to. When Los Angeles activated Pages from the 10-day injured list ahead of Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres -- optioning Eliezer Alfonzo in a corresponding move -- it brought an end to a month-long absence caused by a fractured left hand. With just six regular-season game
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers got their center fielder back on Tuesday, but they aren't expecting Andy Pages to immediately pick up where he left off at the plate. And right now, they don't necessarily need him to.
When Los Angeles activated Pages from the 10-day injured list ahead of Tuesday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres -- optioning Eliezer Alfonzo in a corresponding move -- it brought an end to a month-long absence caused by a fractured left hand. With just six regular-season games remaining before the postseason, Pages’ primary task isn't carrying the offense. It's solidifying the outfield defense.
Pages sustained the fracture on Aug. 21 and underwent a minor surgical procedure to insert a compression screw, an intervention designed to accelerate the bone's healing process. While his recovery stayed on track medically, his physical buildup happened almost entirely in isolation.
Because the Triple-A season concluded over the weekend and internal live-pitching options were unavailable at Dodger Stadium, Pages did not face live arms before being thrown back into Major League action. The Dodgers' Minor League affiliates were deep into playoff runs, and injured internal arms were not far enough along to throw live batting practice, leaving Pages to prepare solely through machine work and a simulated game on Saturday.
Front-hand fractures are notoriously difficult for hitters to bounce back from immediately, as the lead hand controls bat path and turn-through at contact. Because of those physical constraints and the lack of live game reps, expectations for Pages' offensive production over this final week are tempered. Before going down, he was having a standout season, batting .272 (including a .288 mark in August) with an .796 OPS and tying Shohei Ohtani for the team lead with 80 RBIs.
Replicating that midseason rhythm at the plate right away is an unrealistic expectation. But while the Dodgers expect his timing against Major League pitching to take a few games to surface, his defensive value is immediate and undeniable.
According to Statcast metrics on Baseball Savant, Pages ranks in the 94th percentile among qualified defenders with eight outs above average. He has transformed center field into a strength for Los Angeles. In the postseason, where run prevention often dictates close games, having a trusted glove in center field provides a massive floor for manager Dave Roberts -- regardless of how the bats fare.
"The defense is a big reason why he’s still a valuable player, even coming off the IL, with the uncertainty of the offense, which we’ll still bet on," manager Dave Roberts said. "But playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important."
Physically, the team feels comfortable throwing him right back into the fire. While Roberts acknowledged on Saturday that balancing Pages' workload over six straight games would require careful monitoring, he noted on Tuesday that Pages' lower-half conditioning puts him in a good spot to play full games right away.
"I think that I feel good with him playing nine," Roberts said. "He's worked real hard on his lower half, his legs, conditioning, all that stuff. So if I have to manage him, we could do that pivot, get him out of there, get somebody in there to play defense, things like that. But I think right now, the thought is for him to play out each game."
